content:
资助机会通知 (NOFO)：在斯威士兰举办 2027 GCTF 研讨会 资助机会通知 (NOFO) 在斯威士兰美国台湾学院举办 2027 G CTF 研讨会 机会编号：GCTF-TAIPEI-FY2 7 -00 1 申请截止日期：202 年 11 月 23 日 6 日晚上 11:59 （台北时间） A. 基本信息 1. 概述 资助方式：合作协议。合作协议包括局或大使馆实质性参与项目的计划实施。下文 C.2 节包含实质性参与的示例。项目实施期限：拟建项目应于202年5月31日前完成 7．本通知视资金情况而定。公共外交部门保留在被认为符合美国政府最佳利益的情况下授予少于或超过所述资金的权利，具体取决于资金的可用性和指定拨款官员的批准。 2. 执行摘要 美国在台协会 (AIT) 公共外交部门 (PDS) 宣布开展一项合作协议公开竞赛，以支持 2027 年第一季度或第二季度在斯威士兰规划和实施全球合作与培训框架 (GCTF) 区域特许经营研讨会。在资金允许的情况下，AIT 打算授予一份约 20 万美元的合作协议来实施该计划。
全球合作与培训框架（GCTF）是一个国际能力建设平台，汇集了政府官员、技术专家、行业代表、学者和民间社会代表，交流实践经验并加强应对区域和全球挑战的合作。GCTF由台湾和美国于2015年成立，此后扩大到包括日本、澳大利亚、加拿大和英国作为合作伙伴。拟议的研讨会“加强南部非洲的网络安全和数字治理”预计将于 2027 年第一季度或第二季度在斯威士兰举行。该计划将重点关注加强网络安全弹性、改善数字治理、保护关键数字基础设施、应对新出现的网络威胁以及促进安全和可信的数字转型。它将为参与者提供一个交流实践经验、确定共同挑战、加强专业网络和区域合作的平台。该研讨会预计将包括来自至少八个非洲国家的代表，特别强调南部非洲的区域参与。第一天预计将有约 60 至 80 名参与者参加，活动内容包括全体讨论、专家演讲和实践交流。
预计第二天将有约 40 名参与者参加，其中可能包括重点技术讨论、互动练习、工作组会议和/或相关现场参观。该计划预计将汇集来自参与非洲国家的政府官员、网络安全和数字治理从业者、技术专家、私营部门代表、学者、民间社会代表和其他相关利益攸关方。来自美国、台湾和其他 GCTF 合作伙伴（包括日本、澳大利亚、加拿大）的主题专家

【原文 English Original】
Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO): Implementation of 2027 GCTF Workshop in Eswatini Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) Implementation of 2027 G CTF Workshop in Eswatini American Institute in Taiwan Opportunity number: GCTF-TAIPEI-FY2 7 -00 1 Application deadline: November 23 , 202 6 , at 11:59 p.m. (Taipei Time)   A. Basic Information 1. Overview Funding Instrument Type: C ooperative agreement . Cooperative agreements include substantial involvement of the bureau or embassy in program implementation of the project. Examples of substantial involvement are included in section C.2 below. Project Performance Period : Proposed projects should be completed by May 31 , 202 7 . This notice is subject to availability of funding. The Public Diplomacy Section reserves the right to award less or more than the funds described under circumstances deemed to be in the best interest of the U.S. government, pending the availability of funds and approval of the designated grants officer. 2. Executive Summary The American Institute in Taiwan (AIT) Public Diplomacy Section (PDS) announces an open competition for a cooperative agreement to support the planning and implementation of a Global Cooperation and Training Framework (GCTF) regional franchise workshop in Eswatini in the first or second quarter of 2027. Subject to the availability of funding, AIT intends to award one cooperative agreement of approximately USD 200,000 to implement this program. The Global Cooperation and Training Framework (GCTF) is an international capacity-building platform that brings together government officials, technical experts, industry representatives, academics, and civil society representatives to exchange practical experiences and strengthen cooperation in addressing regional and global challenges. The GCTF was established by Taiwan and the United States in 2015 and has since expanded to include Japan, Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom as Partners. The proposed workshop, “Strengthening Cybersecurity and Digital Governance in Southern Africa,” is expected to take place in Eswatini during the first or second quarter of 2027. The program will focus on strengthening cybersecurity resilience, improving digital governance, protecting critical digital infrastructure, addressing emerging cyber threats, and promoting secure and trusted digital transformation. It will provide a platform for participants to exchange practical experiences, identify common challenges, and strengthen professional networks and regional cooperation. The workshop is expected to include representatives from at least eight African countries, with a particular emphasis on regional participation from Southern Africa. Approximately 60 to 80 participants are expected to participate in the first day of the program, which will feature plenary discussions, expert presentations, and practical exchanges. A smaller group of approximately 40 participants is expected to participate in the second day, which may include focused technical discussions, interactive exercises, working-group sessions, and/or relevant site visits. The program is expected to bring together government officials, cybersecurity and digital governance practitioners, technical experts, private-sector representatives, academics, civil society representatives, and other relevant stakeholders from participating African countries. Subject-matter experts from the United States, Taiwan, and other GCTF Partners, including Japan, Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom, may also be invited to contribute relevant international expertise and practical experience. The selected recipient will serve as AIT’s implementation partner and will be responsible for comprehensive program and logistical support, including venue and lodging coordination, participant management, travel arrangements for designated participants and speakers, ground transportation, interpretation and audiovisual services, workshop materials, vendor coordination, monitoring and evaluation, and required grant reporting. Travel expenses for U.S. Government officials invited by the U.S. Government and Taiwan-supported speakers will be funded separately and should not be included in the recipient’s proposed budget. AIT and GCTF partners will provide overall policy guidance, strategic direction, and substantive oversight throughout program planning and implementation. Eligible applicants include nonprofit organizations, educational institutions, professional associations, think tanks, private-sector organizations with relevant international program management experience, public international organizations where eligible under applicable U.S. Government regulations, and other eligible organizations with demonstrated capacity to organize international conferences or capacity-building programs and administer U.S. Government assistance awards. This cooperative agreement is intended to strengthen practical cybersecurity capacity and digital governance cooperation in Southern Africa, expand professional and institutional connections among participating countries, and advance the GCTF as a platform for practical international capacity building, technical exchange, and sustained regional cooperation. B. Eligibility 1. Eligible Applicants The following organizations are eligible to apply: Not-for-profit organizations , including non-governmental organizations (NGOs), think tanks, and civil society organizations Educational institutions , including universities and research institutions Professional associations and nonprofit organizations with demonstrated experience managing international conferences or capacity-building programs Private-sector organizations with demonstrated experience organizing international conferences or implementing international exchange programs Public international organizations , where eligible under applicable U.S. Government regulations Organizations may sub-contract with other entities, but only one entity, from the eligible categories of organizations listed above, can be the prime recipient of the award. When sub-contracting with other entities, the responsibilities of each entity must be clearly defined in the proposal. For more information on the difference between sub-contract and sub-recipient, please refer to 2 CFR 200 .331 . 2. Cost Sharing or Matching Cost sharing is not required . 3. Other Eligibility Requirements All organizations must have a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) issued via SAM.gov as well as a valid registration in SAM.gov. Please see Section D.3 for more information. Individuals are not required to have a UEI or be registered in SAM.gov. Applicants are only allowed to submit one proposal per organization. If more than one proposal is submitted from an organization, all proposals from that institution will be considered ineligible for funding. 4. This opportunity will not support: Projects relating to partisan political activity; Charitable or development activities; including direct social services such as medical, psychological, and/or humanitarian support Construction projects; Projects that support specific religious activities; Fund-raising campaigns; Lobbying for specific legislation or programs Scientific research or surveys; Commercial projects; Projects intended primarily for the growth or institutional development of the organization; Projects that duplicate existing projects; Illegal activities C. Program Description 1. Project Background, Goals, and Objectives Project Background The Global Cooperation and Training Framework (GCTF) is an international capacity-building platform established by Taiwan and the United States in 2015. Japan joined as a full partner in 2019, followed by Australia in 2021, Canada in 2023, and the United Kingdom in 2025. Through workshops and other capacity-building activities, GCTF brings together government officials, technical experts, industry representatives, and civil society representatives to exchange practical experience, strengthen professional networks, and develop approaches to shared regional and global challenges. As governments and societies become increasingly dependent on digital technologies and interconnected systems, cybersecurity and effective digital governance have become important elements of economic development, public-service delivery, critical infrastructure resilience, and public trust. Recent research documents that scam syndicates displaced from Southeast Asian epicenters, including Myanmar, Laos, and Cambodia, are actively pivoting to Africa, with documented raids in nine African countries and growing evidence of scam infrastructure, including online gambling platforms used as cover for fraud operations, gray business Telegram groups openly advertising scam facilities, and unregulated cryptocurrency services establishing footholds across the continent. Countries across Southern Africa face evolving cybersecurity and cybercrime challenges while also seeking to expand digital services, strengthen institutional capacity, and develop governance frameworks that support secure and trusted digital transformation. The proposed GCTF regional workshop in Eswatini will provide a platform for government officials, cybersecurity and the digital governance practitioners, technical experts, private-sector representatives, academics, civil society representatives, and other relevant stakeholders from across Africa to exchange practical experiences and strengthen professional and institutional connections. The workshop is expected to include representatives from at least eight African countries, with particular emphasis on participation from Southern Africa. The program will draw on expertise and practical experience from participating African countries as well as the United States, Taiwan, and other GCTF partners, as appropriate. Through expert presentations, policy and technical discussions, interactive exchanges, and other practical activities, the workshop will address shared challenges and identify approaches that participating countries may adapt to their respective national and institutional contexts. Strengthening cybersecurity capacity and secure digital governance in Southern Africa also advances U.S. security and economic interests. Cyber threats, cyber-enabled crime, and vulnerabilities in interconnected digital systems increasingly cross-national borders and can affect American citizens, businesses, and critical infrastructure. By strengthening the ability of partner countries to prevent, identify, respond to, and recover from cyber threats, this program can help reduce vulnerabilities that may be exploited by transnational criminal networks and other malicious cyber actors. The workshop will also strengthen U.S. engagement with African partners on secure and resilient digital ecosystems, promote cooperation and information sharing among governments and technical experts, and expand relationships between African stakeholders and the United States and other GCTF partners. Through practical capacity building and sustained professional networks, the program will support a more secure and resilient regional digital environment while advancing shared interests in cybersecurity, economic security, and trusted digital development. Project Goal: The goal of this project is to strengthen cybersecurity resilience and digital governance capacity in Southern Africa by facilitating practical knowledge exchange, regional cooperation, and sustained professional engagement among participating countries and international partners, while advancing shared U.S. and partner interests in a more secure, resilient, and trusted digital environment. Project Objectives: The project will pursue the following objectives: Strengthen Cybersecurity Capacity and Resilience: Enhance participants’ knowledge of practical approaches to preventing, preparing for, responding to, and recovering from cybersecurity threats and incidents, with a specific focus on basic cyber hygiene, national cyber resilience, digital trust, and the development of a secure digital ecosystem aligned with global standards and best practices. Advance Effective and Secure Digital Governance: Promote the exchange of policies, practices, institutional approaches, and lessons learned that support secure, trusted, resilient, and inclusive digital governance and digital transformation. Promote Regional Cooperation and Information Sharing: Strengthen professional and institutional connections among participating African countries and encourage greater cross-border cooperation, information sharing, and coordination in addressing shared cybersecurity and digital governance challenges. Facilitate Practical International Exchange: Connect African policymakers and practitioners with relevant expertise and practical experience from participating African countries, the United States, Taiwan, and other GCTF partner countries, including Japan, Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom, as appropriate to the workshop agenda. Support Sustainable Professional Networks and Follow-on Cooperation: Encourage participants to identify practical opportunities for continued professional engagement, knowledge sharing, and future cooperation beyond the workshop. 2. Substantial Involvement This award will require substantial involvement from the American Institute in Taiwan (AIT ) and the U . S . Embassy in Eswatini . AIT will approve all key aspects of the workshop, including but not limited to venue selection, flight and hotel arrangements, ground transportation, lodging, visual designs, agenda, site visit locations, speaker and participant lists, catering and menus, conference room layout, lighting, and audio-visual setup. D. Application Contents and Format Please follow all instructions below carefully. Proposals that do not meet the requirements of this announcement or fail to comply with the stated requirements will be ineligible. Content of Application Please ensure: The proposal clearly addresses the goals and objectives of this funding opportunity All documents are in English All budgets are in U.S. dollars All pages are numbered, including budgets and attachments All documents are formatted to fit 8 ½ x 11 paper All documents are single-spaced, 14-point New Times Roman font, with 1-inch margins. Captions and footnotes may be 10-point New Times Roman font. Font sizes in charts and tables, including the budget, can be reformatted to fit within 1 page width. All applicant authorized signatures are provided where indicated on the various, required forms. The following documents are required: 1. Mandatory application forms SF-424 (Application for Federal Assistance – organizations) at https://grants.gov/ or https://www.ait.org.tw / . SF-424A (Budget Information for Non-Construction programs) at https://grants.gov/ or https://www.ait.org.tw / . SF-424B (Assurances for Non-Construction programs) at https://grants.gov/ or https://www.ait.org.tw / . (note: the SF-424B is only required for individuals, organizations exempt from registration, and for organizations not required to fully register in https://sam.gov/ ) 2. Proposal (10 pages maximum) The proposal should contain sufficient information that anyone not familiar with it would understand exactly what the applicant wants to do. You may use your own proposal format, but it must include all the items below. Proposal Summary: Short narrative that outlines the proposed project, including project objectives and anticipated impact. (Attachment: Recommended Proposal Template ). Introduction to the Organization : A description of past and present operations, showing ability to carry out the program, including information on all previous grants from the State Department and/or U.S. government agencies as well as experience with and expertise in areas related to those described in the NOFO. Applicants are encouraged, but not required, to use the attached Applicant Organization Information Survey form to provide this information (Attachment : Recommended Applicant Organization Information (AOI) Survey Template ). If the applicant chooses not to use the attached form, all of the requested information from the form will still need to be addressed in the application package. Problem Statement: Clear, concise and well-supported statement of the problem to be addressed and why the proposed program is needed Program Methods, Design, Activities, and Deliverables: The “goals” describe what the program is intended to achieve. The “objectives” refer to the intermediate accomplishments on the way to the goals. These should be achievable and measurable. Describe the program activities and how they will help achieve the objectives. Proposed Project Schedule and Timeline: The proposed timeline for the program activities. Include the dates, times, and locations of planned activities and events. Key Personnel: Names, titles, roles and experience/qualifications of key personnel involved in the program. What proportion of their time will be used in support of this program? Project Partners: List the names and type of involvement of key partner organizations and sub-awardees (if applicable). Future Funding or Sustainability: Applicant’s plan for continuing the program beyond the grant period, or the availability of other resources, if applicable. Monitoring & Evaluation Plan: Proposals must include a draft Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Performance Monitoring Plan (PMP). The M&E PMP should show how applicants intend to measure and demonstrate progress towards the project’s objectives and goals. The key components to the PMP are as follows: Monitoring and Evaluation Narrative: In narrative form, applicants should describe how they intend to monitor and evaluate the activities of their award. In addition, the applicant should describe any M&E processes, including key personnel, management structure (where M&E fits into the overall program’s staff structure), technology, and as well provide a brief budget narrative explaining any line-item expenditures for M&E listed in the program’s budget. If the proposal is from a prior grantee, the proposal discusses how the grantee has adapted, improved or otherwise modified their approach based on learning from previous experience. This narrative is limited to two pages. Theory of Change Diagram: Applicants are expected to submit either a Theory of Change diagram or an If-Then Statement that illustrates how project activities will lead to intended outcomes. Monitoring and Evaluation Datasheet: The applicant must include their proposed activities and their expected outputs and outcomes as well as the goals and objectives as written in the NOFO. The datasheet’s purpose is to explicitly illustrate how a project’s activities lead to tangible results (such as increased beneficiary skills, knowledge, or attitudes) that ultimately address a PDS objective. The selected applicant’s M&E PMP is subject to review and approval before any award will be issued under this NOFO. The selected applicant will be required to work with the Public Diplomacy Section’s Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist to ensure the applicant’s M&E PMP achieves an expected level of expertise and meets PDS objectives. Expenses directly associated with monitoring and evaluation are considered allowable. The suggested template includes a space to list the portion of the total budget amount directly associated with monitoring and evaluation activities. 3. Review Criteria Criteria: Each application submitted under this announcement will be evaluated and rated on the basis of the criteria enumerated below. The criteria are designed to assess the quality of the proposed project, and to determine the likelihood of its success. Quality and Feasibility of the Program Idea – 20 points: The program idea should be innovative and well developed, with sufficient detail about how p roject activities will be carried out. The proposals should demonstrate originality and outline clear, achievable objectives that align directly with the priorities and requirements of the NOFO . The proposal includes a reasonable implementation timeline, and the project scope is appropriate and clearly defined. The project will positively impact America’s reputation among foreign government partners. The project will positively impact American’s reputation among foreign publics. The proposal does not include any activities contrary to the following Executive Orders: Executive Order 14173: “Ending Illegal Discrimination and Restoring Merit-Based Opportunity Executive Order 14287: “Protecting American Communities from Criminal Aliens” Executive Order 14168: Defending Women from Gender Ideology Extremism and Restoring Biological Truth to the Federal Government Organizational Capacity and Record on Previous Grants – 20 points: The project proposal demonstrates that the organization has sufficient expertise, skills, and human resources to implement the project, including internal contr ols in place to manage federal funds. The organization demonstrates that it has a clear understanding of the underlying issue that the project will address. The organization demonstrates capacity for successful planning and responsible fiscal management. This includes a financial management system , a bank account , and if applicable, satisfactory audit findings. Applicants who have received grant funds previously have been compliant with applicable rules and regulations , including the Award Provisions and Standard Terms and Conditions. Where partners are described, the applicant details each partner’s respective role and provides curriculum vitae (CVs) for persons responsible for the project and financial administration. Proposed personnel, institutional resources, and partners are adequate and appropriate. Project Planning/Ability to Achieve Objectives – 25 points: The project plan is well developed, with sufficient detail about how activities will be carried out. The proposal specifies target audiences, participant recruitment, and geographic areas of implementation. The proposal outlines clear, achievable objectives. The proposal includes a reasonable implementation timeline. The project scope is appropriate and clearly defined. Budget – 15 points: The budget and narrative justification are sufficiently detailed. The budget demonstrates that the organization has devoted time to accurately determine expenses associated with the project instead of providing rough estimates. Costs are reasonable in relation to the proposed activities and anticipated results. The results and proposed outcomes justify the total cost of the project. Budget items are reasonable, allowable, and allocable. Monitoring and Evaluation – 10 points: There is a complete and thorough draft submission of a M&E Performance Monitoring Plan (PMP). Funded projects will have their plans finalized during the negotiation phase, and monitoring plans may be subject to periodic updates throughout the life of the project. content:
USNI 新闻图 这些是根据海军和公开数据，截至 2026 年 11 月 9 日，美国海军在世界各地部署的航母打击群和两栖战备群的大致位置。如果 CSG 或 ARG 正在进行分类操作，图表会反映主力舰的位置。 2026 年 10 月 11 日，在日本，航空水手长的大副飞行员 Tykwon Young（右）和航空水手长的大副飞行员 Saabirah Parker 在停泊在佐世保湾的美国级两栖攻击舰的黎波里号 (LHA-7) 的飞行甲板上涂上小白眼。美国海军照片 USS 的黎波里号 (LHA-7) 停泊在日本佐世保港口。 2026 年 11 月 5 日，在日本海，第 13 海军陆战队远征队第 2/4 营登陆队的一名海军陆战队员在黄蜂级两栖攻击舰马金岛号 (LHD-8) 上进行静态快速绳索训练。美国海军陆战队照片 据舰艇观察员称，美国海军陆战队照片两栖攻击舰马金岛号 (LHD-8) 于周六从日本横须贺出发。马金岛两栖准备大队包括马金岛、安克雷奇号航空母舰 (LPD-23)、约翰·P·穆萨号航空母舰 (LPD-26) 和已上船的第 13 海军陆战队远征部队，目前正在日本海执行任务。 2026 年 10 月 22 日，来自新墨西哥州阿尔伯克基的加勒比海船体维护技术员二等迈克尔·布卢瓦斯三世 (Michael Bloise III) 在加勒比海航行的自由级濒海战斗舰明尼阿波利斯-圣保罗号 (LCS-21) 上进行焊接操作。
美国海军照片 濒海战斗舰明尼阿波利斯-圣保罗号 (LCS-21) 正在加勒比海中部作业。自由级濒海战斗舰驻扎在佛罗里达州梅波特海军基地。在地中海，三级内政通信电工 Micah Lee 在与刘易斯和克拉克级干货船 USNS Medgar Evers (T-AKE-13) 登上阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰 USS 进行海上补给之前检查通信设备巴尔克利号（DDG-84）在地中海，2026 年 10 月 22 日。美国海军照片 在地中海执行任务的独立部署的导弹驱逐舰包括：奥斯卡·奥斯汀号航空母舰（DDG-79），母港为罗塔海军基地。 USS Bulkeley (DDG-84)，母港为罗塔海军基地。美国海军保罗·伊格纳修斯号 (DDG-117)，母港为罗塔海军基地。斯托特号 (DDG-55) 母港位于弗吉尼亚州诺福克海军基地。2026 年 10 月 6 日，美国海军水手在阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰奥斯卡·奥斯汀号 (DDG-79) 上的驾驶室里站岗，当时该舰正通过苏伊士运河。美国海军照片 有两艘导弹驱逐舰在红海执行任务： USS Jason Dunham (DDG-109)，母港为佛罗里达州梅波特海军基地。美国海军冈萨雷斯号 (DDG-66)，母港为弗吉尼亚州诺福克海军基地。2026 年 11 月 7 日，在阿拉伯海，乔治·华盛顿号航空母舰 (CVN-73) 与刘易斯和克拉克级干货和弹药舰沃利·施艾拉号 (T-AKE-8) 一起进行海上补给。

title: Launch Preview: Starship, Vulcan, and Electron launches scheduled for busy week
zh_title: 发射预览：Starship、Vulcan 和 Electron 计划在繁忙的一周发射
summary: 来自四个国家的七枚火箭将于本周发射。星际飞船将尝试其迄今为止最重要的任务，而猎鹰 9 号将为美国太空军发射一对机密有效载荷。联合发射联盟计划让 Vulcan 执行其返回飞行任务，而 Electron 则将完成第 100 次任务，具有里程碑意义。在国际上，中国和韩国将分别发射未知的有效载荷和演示任务。猎鹰 9 号 | USSF-627（“R-5”）本周首次发射将由猎鹰 9 号火箭提供机密有效载荷
content:
来自四个国家的七枚火箭将于本周发射。星际飞船将尝试其迄今为止最重要的任务，而猎鹰 9 号将为美国太空军发射一对机密有效载荷。联合发射联盟计划让 Vulcan 执行其返回飞行任务，而 Electron 则将完成第 100 次任务，具有里程碑意义。在国际上，中国和韩国将分别发射未知的有效载荷和演示任务。猎鹰 9 号 | USSF-627（“R-5”）本周首次发射将由猎鹰 9 号火箭为美国太空军 (USSF) 提供机密有效载荷。该任务被指定为 USSF-627，最初计划于 11 月 8 日星期日发射。猎鹰 9 号现定于太平洋标准时间 11 月 9 日星期一晚上 7:07（世界标准时间 10 月 10 日 03:07）从范登堡太空部队基地 (VSFB) 的 4 号东部太空发射综合体 (SLC-4E) 起飞，距太平洋标准时间晚上 11:03 (07:03) 的窗口期已过去四分钟。 UTC 时间 11 月 10 日）。由于有效载荷的机密性质，卫星的确切数量尚不清楚。一些指标表明，基于猎鹰 9 号第二级的降落区，星盾将进行发射。 Starshield是为美国政府打造的Starlink版本，其主要客户是USSF、国家侦察办公室和太空发展局。范登堡太空部队基地 4E 号航天发射场发射台上的猎鹰 9 号火箭。
（图片来源：SpaceX）Falcon 9 是一款两级、70 m 高、部分可重复使用的火箭，第一级使用九个 Merlin 1D 海平面发动机，第二级使用单个真空优化的 Merlin 1D。Falcon 9 的第一级降落在自主无人机船上或着陆点，其整流罩在飞行后回收并重复使用。两个阶段都使用液体煤油和液氧作为推进剂。助推器 B1103 将在其第七次飞行中支持这项任务。此前，该助推器已支持 NROL-179、第一批传输层 A 和 E 以及三个星链任务的发射。猎鹰 9 号将搭乘 SpaceX 的无人机“当然我仍然爱你”着陆。米尔 |演示飞行 11 月 10 日星期二，韩国计划发射韩国军方小型卫星运载火箭和平号的第二次飞行。继 2023 年 12 月进行了不包括第二级的试飞之后，此次发射将是全尺寸火箭的首次轨道飞行。启动窗口于 05:00 UTC 开始，并延长至 09:00 UTC。和平号是一款四级固体燃料运载火箭，第四级采用液体燃料，可实现精确入轨。 2023 年 12 月飞行的版本能够运载 700 公斤至近地轨道，该版本疑似能够运载 1,000 公斤左右。长征2D |有效载荷未知 11 月 11 日星期三，长征 2D (CZ-2D) 火箭计划从酒泉卫星发射中心发射升空。
目前，发射计划于 11:40 UTC 进行，距离 11:32 UTC 开启并持续到 12:05 UTC 的窗口还有 8 分钟的时间。CZ-2D 将向轨道发射未知有效载荷。 CZ-2D 是一款两级、41 米高的运载火箭，能够向近地轨道 (LEO) 发射 3,500 公斤的重量。 CZ-2D的第一级和第二级均由四氧化二氮和不对称二甲肼提供动力，这两种推进剂都是自燃推进剂。周三的发射将是长征二号丁的第 107 次发射，也是 2026 年的第六次发射。快舟 11 |有效载荷未知本周第二个也是最后一个预定的中国任务

【原文 English Original】
Seven rockets from four countries are set to launch this week. Starship is set to attempt its most consequential mission yet, while Falcon 9 is set to launch a pair of classified payloads for the United States Space Force. The United Launch Alliance is scheduled to fly Vulcan on its return-to-flight mission, and Electron is set to reach a milestone 100th mission. Internationally, China and South Korea are set to launch an unknown payload and a demonstration mission, respectively. Falcon 9 | USSF-627 (“R-5”) The first launch of the week will feature Falcon 9 delivering a classified payload for the United States Space Force (USSF). The mission, designated USSF-627, was initially scheduled to launch on Sunday, Nov. 8. Falcon 9 is now set to take off from Space Launch Complex 4 East (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB) on Monday, Nov. 9, at 7:07 PM PST (03:07 UTC on Nov. 10), four minutes into a window that extends until 11:03 PM PST (07:03 UTC on Nov. 10). Due to the classified nature of the payload, the exact quantity of satellites is unknown. Some indicators suggest a Starshield launch, based on drop zones for Falcon 9’s second stage. Starshield is a version of Starlink built for the United States government, with its primary customers being the USSF, National Reconnaissance Office, and the Space Development Agency. A Falcon 9 on the launch pad at Space Launch Complex-4E on Vandenberg Space Force Base. (Credit: SpaceX) Falcon 9 is a two-stage, 70 m-tall, partially reusable rocket that uses nine Merlin 1D sea-level engines on its first stage and a single vacuum-optimized Merlin 1D on its second stage. Falcon 9’s first stage lands either aboard an autonomous droneship or at a landing site, with its fairings being recovered and reused after flight. Both stages utilize liquid kerosene and liquid oxygen as propellants. Booster B1103 will be supporting this mission on its seventh flight. Previously, this booster has supported the launches of NROL-179, Tranche 1 Transport Layers A and E, and three Starlink missions. Falcon 9 will land downrange aboard SpaceX’s droneship Of Course I Still Love You . Mir | Demo Flight On Tuesday, Nov. 10, South Korea is set to launch the second flight of Mir, the South Korean military’s small satellite launch vehicle. This launch is set to be the first orbital flight of the full-scale rocket, following a test flight in December 2023 that did not include the second stage. The launch window opens at 05:00 UTC and extends until 09:00 UTC. Mir is a four-stage, solid-fuel launch vehicle with a liquid-fueled fourth stage for precise orbital insertion. The version that flew in December 2023 was capable of 700 kg to LEO, with this version suspected to be capable of around 1,000 kg. Chang Zheng 2D | Unknown Payload On Wednesday, Nov. 11, a Chang Zheng 2D (CZ-2D) rocket is scheduled to launch out of the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center. The launch is currently scheduled for 11:40 UTC, eight minutes into a window that opens at 11:32 UTC and extends until 12:05 UTC. CZ-2D will deliver an unknown payload into orbit. CZ-2D is a two-stage, 41 m-tall launch vehicle capable of delivering 3,500 kg to low-Earth orbit (LEO). CZ-2D’s first and second stages are both powered by dinitrogen tetroxide and unsymmetrical dimethyl hydrazine, both hypergolic propellants. Wednesday’s launch will be the 107th overall for CZ-2D, and sixth in 2026. Kuaizhou 11 | Unknown Payload The second and final scheduled Chinese mission of the week will see a Kuaizhou 11 rocket launch on Thursday, Nov. 12. Liftoff is set for 19:50 UTC from Site 95A at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, during a 45-minute launch window. Kuaizhou 11 is a four-stage Chinese rocket manufactured by the China Aerospace Science and Industry Corporation. Standing 25.3 m tall, the rocket can loft 1,500 kg to LEO with a liftoff thrust of 1,250 kN. This mission will be the eighth overall Kuaizhou 11 mission and the fourth of 2026. Vulcan VC6L | Amazon Leo (LV-01) United Launch Alliance’s (ULA) Vulcan rocket is set to launch on Friday, Nov. 13, from Space Launch Complex 41 (SLC-41) at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station. The 30-minute launch window opens at 12:54 PM EST (17:54 UTC). This will be the first flight of Vulcan in over nine months, following the ejection of one of Vulcan’s GEM-63XL solid rocket boosters at T+69 seconds on the USSF-87 mission. Flying aboard Vulcan will be a stack of 40 Amazon Leo satellites for Amazon’s Leo satellite internet constellation, a rival to SpaceX’s Starlink. A ULA Vulcan (USSF-87) sits next to a SpaceX Crew Dragon (Crew-12). (Credit: Tyler Gray for NSF) Vulcan is a two-stage launch vehicle with a range of launch configurations. Vulcan’s first stage is powered by two BE-4 engines built by Blue Origin, running on liquid methane and liquid oxygen propellants. Its second stage, Centaur V, is powered by twin RL10C engines running on liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen. Centaur V can be configured as Centaur LEO, High Energy, or Endurance. Vulcan can also be configured with solid rocket boosters to augment liftoff thrust, with options ranging from zero to two, four, or six boosters. The payload is encapsulated by either a short (15.5 m) or a long (21.3 m) fairing. Vulcan will debut the Vulcan VC6L variant, designated by six solid boosters and the long fairing option. Vulcan will debut the LEO-optimized Centaur V, which is 1.94 m smaller than the existing Centaur V High Energy, which has flown on all previous Vulcan launches. Additionally, this flight is a certification flight of this Vulcan configuration for the United States Space Force. Amazon Leo (LV-01) will be the first of 38 scheduled for Vulcan and the fifth overall mission for Vulcan. Starship | Flight 15 / Starlink Group 31-2 Pending regulatory approval, Starship is set to fly its next, and most significant, mission no earlier than Friday, Nov. 13, at 4:45 PM CST (22:45 UTC). The launch window extends until 6:00 PM CST (00:00 UTC on Nov. 14). Flight 15 will feature two notable events: the first booster-catch attempt since Flight 8, following stage separation, and the first attempt to catch the ship, roughly 22 hours after liftoff. Starship is a two-stage, super-heavy-lift launch vehicle capable of lofting an estimated 100 tonnes. The first stage, named Super Heavy, features 33 Raptor 3 engines, running off of liquid methane and liquid oxygen propellants. The second stage, named Starship, features six Raptor 3 engines, three sea-level and three vacuum-optimized, also running off of liquid methane and liquid oxygen. Flying on Flight 15 will be Ship 42 and Booster 22, both on their first flights. Flight 15 is expected to deliver 26 Starlink v3 satellites to LEO. Like Flight 14, three of these satellites will feature imaging capabilities for imaging the heat shield of Starship in orbit. Flight 15 will be the 15th full-stack launch of Starship and the fourth for the system’s V3 configuration. Falcon 9 | USSF-317 (“R-6”) Falcon 9 is set to fly again on Friday, Nov. 13, from VSFB with another USSF mission. The designation for this flight is USSF-317. The launch window opens at 8:09 PM PST (04:09 UTC on Nov. 14), and lasts for four hours. This mission will fly another unknown quantity of presumed Starshield satellites to LEO. Booster B1100 will support this mission, marking its 11th flight. This booster has previously supported NROL-105, USSF-385, and eight Starlink missions. B1100 will land downrange aboard SpaceX’s droneship Of Course I Still Love You . Electron during its 95th launch “Happily Ever Faster.” Credit: Rocket Lab) Electron | The Mountain God Rises The last scheduled launch of the week will see Rocket Lab’s Electron launch from the Mahia Peninsula in New Zealand on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 05:30 UTC. This flight of Electron, named “The Mountain God Rises,” will deliver another iQPS satellite into LEO for iQPS’s synthetic aperture radar constellation (SAR). SAR is used to image the surface of the Earth and can penetrate through cloud layers. Electron is a two-stage small-lift vehicle capable of delivering up to 300 kg to LEO and 200 kg to Sun-synchronous orbit. The vehicle is fueled by liquid kerosene and liquid oxygen, which powers nine Rutherford engines on the first stage and a single vacuum-optimized Rutherford on the second stage. This mission will serve as Electron’s 100th overall mission — a notable milestone for the small rocket that first flew in 2017. In addition, this mission will serve as the 269th orbital launch attempt worldwide in 2026. ( Lead Image: Falcon 9 launches from Florida. Credit: Julia Bergeron for NSF) The post Launch Preview: Starship, Vulcan, and Electron launches scheduled for busy week appeared first on NASASpaceFlight.com .

title: China Lifts The Veil On Its GJ-11 Mysterious Dragon Stealth UCAV
zh_title: 中国揭开GJ-11神秘龙隐形无人机的面纱
summary: 中国为我们提供了迄今为止最清晰的 GJ-11 隐形无人战斗机 (UCAV) 展示，新的官方镜头揭示了这款飞翼无人机以前未见过的细节，包括其内部武器舱、起落架、安装在机头的传感器以及独特的排气装置。与此同时，中国人民解放军空军 (PLAAF) 还声称，GJ-11 已经完成了首次实弹打击任务，取得了成功。这有点令人费解，因为无人战斗机已经进行了多年的测试架次，包括在前方
content:
中国为我们提供了迄今为止最清晰的 GJ-11 隐形无人战斗机 (UCAV) 展示，新的官方镜头揭示了这款飞翼无人机以前未见过的细节，包括其内部武器舱、起落架、安装在机头的传感器以及独特的排气装置。与此同时，中国人民解放军空军 (PLAAF) 还声称，GJ-11 已经完成了首次实弹打击任务，取得了成功。这有点令人费解，因为无人作战飞机多年来已经进行了多次测试，包括在前沿作战地点，而且在此之前几乎无法想象是否进行过实弹武器投送。也许这是在转换过程中丢失某些东西的情况，例如使用新的内部传感器或新型武器发射。跑道上 GJ-11 的正面视图。 PLA screencap 这段视频昨天由中国国家电视台中央电视台播出，距离中国人民解放军空军成立 77 周年还有两天。随附的报告提供了有关该飞机预期任务集的更多详细信息，包括空袭和压制敌方防空系统（SEAD），以及它与有人战斗机的有人与无人编队（MUM-T）行动的整合。
新披露的信息让公众对 GJ-11 的配置有了最全面的了解，并进一步了解中国打算如何使用这款名为“玄龙”的隐形飞翼飞机。GJ-11 起飞。 PLA screencap 仔细观察 GJ-11 最暴露的视图之一显示了 GJ-11 的底面，清楚地暴露了其两个内部武器舱。腹侧舱位于飞机的混合翼体内，具有独立的门组，具有独特的锯齿状边缘——这是低可观察性飞机的常见特征。舱室的内部布局和尺寸仍不清楚，飞机可容纳的武器的精确范围也不清楚。然而，每个舱室似乎可以容纳至少 1,000 磅级武器，甚至可能容纳 2,000 磅级武器。 #GTMilitaryWatch 央视新闻军事频道周一发布了新镜头，以多角度特写镜头展示了中国人民解放军 (PLA) 空军的 GJ-11 隐形无人机。它还透露，空军首批自行训练的两架女无人机… pic.twitter.com/PPVmws9DJJ —《环球时报》（@globaltimesnews）2026年11月9日 据央视报道，这两个舱可携带多种空对地/水面弹药。
此前，中国航空工业集团公司 (AVIC) 在 2021 年中国航展上展示的 GJ-11 模型中曾透露过武器舱配置，但新的镜头可以更好地展示实际飞机。机库中 GJ-11 的正面视图，武器舱门部分打开。 PLA screencap 内部武器架是 GJ-11 隐蔽性设计的核心，使其能够携带弹药，而不会受到与外部挂架和挂具相关的雷达信号（和空气动力学）影响。此前于 2025 年 11 月发布的视频显示，GJ-11 正在飞行，起落架仍处于伸出状态。然而，其中一个新序列显示飞机起飞，随后的侧视图和后视图捕捉到了其起落架在升空后收回的情况。起落架本身非常坚固，包括一个重型起落架

【原文 English Original】
China has provided us with the clearest look yet at its GJ-11 stealth uncrewed combat aerial vehicle (UCAV), with new official footage revealing previously unseen details of the flying-wing drone, including its internal weapons bays, landing gear, nose-mounted sensor installation, and distinctive exhaust arrangement. The release also comes alongside a claim from the People’s Liberation Army Air Force (PLAAF) that the GJ-11 has completed its first live-fire strike mission, scoring a hit. This is somewhat puzzling, since the UCAV has racked up test sorties for years already, including at forward operating locations, and it seems almost inconceivable that a live weapons delivery would not have been conducted before now. Perhaps this is a case of something being lost in translation, such as the use of a new internal sensor or a new type of weapon delivery. Head-on view of a GJ-11 on the runway. PLA screencap The footage, broadcast by Chinese state television’s CCTV yesterday, comes two days ahead of the 77th anniversary of the founding of the PLAAF. Accompanying reporting provides additional details about the aircraft’s intended mission set, including airstrikes and suppression of enemy air defenses (SEAD), as well as its integration into manned-unmanned teaming (MUM-T) operations with crewed fighters. The new disclosures offer the most comprehensive public look yet at the GJ-11’s configuration and provide further insight into how China intends to employ the stealthy flying-wing aircraft, which is named Xuanlong — Chinese for Mystery Dragon. A GJ-11 takes off. PLA screencap A closer look at the GJ-11 One of the most revealing views shows the underside of the GJ-11, clearly exposing its two internal weapons bays. Located within the aircraft’s blended wing-body, the ventral bays have separate sets of doors with distinctive serrated edges — a common feature on low-observable aircraft. The internal arrangement and dimensions of the bays remain unclear, as does the precise range of weapons the aircraft can accommodate. However, it would appear likely that each bay can accommodate at least a 1,000-pound-class and likely a 2,000-pound-class weapon. #GTMilitaryWatch CCTV News military channel released new footage on Monday offering a close-up, multi-angle look at the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Air Force's GJ-11 stealth drone. It also revealed that two of the Air Force's first batch of self-trained female drone… pic.twitter.com/PPVmws9DJJ — Global Times (@globaltimesnews) November 9, 2026 According to CCTV , the two bays can carry a variety of air-to-ground/surface munitions. The weapons bay configuration had previously been revealed in a model of the GJ-11 displayed by the Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC) at Airshow China in 2021, but the new footage provides a much better look at the actual aircraft. Head-on view of a GJ-11 in the hangar, with the weapons bay doors partially open. PLA screencap Internal weapons carriage is central to the GJ-11’s low-observable design, allowing it to carry munitions without the radar signature (and aerodynamic) penalties associated with external pylons and stores. Previous footage released in November 2025 showed the GJ-11 in flight with its landing gear remaining extended. However, one of the new sequences shows the aircraft taking off, with subsequent side and rear views capturing its landing gear retracting after liftoff. The landing gear itself is notably robust, including a heavy-duty twin-wheel nose unit. With that in mind, it may be the same landing gear as used in the GJ-21, a naval variant capable of operating from aircraft carriers and big-deck assault ships. A GJ-11 retracts its landing gear on takeoff. PLA screencap The new imagery also offers a closer look at a trapezoidal glazed fairing beneath the nose. This appears consistent with an electro-optical/infrared (EO/IR) sensor installation. Its precise configuration and capabilities have not been disclosed, but it’s worth noting that similar-looking installations also appear on the crewed J-20 and J-35 fighters, with these systems apparently being analogous to the electro-optical targeting system, or EOTS, found on the F-35 . If the sensor on the GJ-11 works like an EOTS, it would provide the drone with precision targeting and identification, lasing, as well as a secondary infrared search-and-track emulation function. A view of a GJ-11 showing the undernose EO/IR sensor installation. PLA screencap Perhaps the most distinctive external feature remains the GJ-11’s exhaust arrangement, for what is reported to be a WS-13 turbofan engine. A close-up of the rear of the aircraft shows the flattened exhaust outlet, shielded and integrated into the upper rear portion of the flying-wing airframe. Combined with the dorsal air intake and the absence of conventional exposed engine nozzles, this configuration is intended to reduce the aircraft’s radar and infrared signatures, especially from the most critical view aspects. The GJ-11’s tailless, blended-wing configuration is by now a defining feature of low-observable UCAV designs. Close-up of the tail section of a GJ-11. PLA screencap At least some of the GJ-11s shown have an air data boom on the nose. While normally associated with early flight testing, the GJ-11 is now far beyond that. The booms could still be fitted for some envelope expansion and other flight test work, although it may also simply involve earlier footage. Airstrikes and suppression of enemy air defenses Beyond the new imagery, one of the more interesting aspects of the CCTV coverage is its description of the GJ-11’s intended operational role. The broadcaster identified airstrikes and SEAD among the aircraft’s mission sets. The latter is particularly significant, as penetrating or operating within heavily defended airspace to locate and suppress or destroy enemy air defense systems is the most dangerous mission for a crewed combat aircraft. A stealthy uncrewed aircraft could contribute to these operations by carrying precision-guided weapons into more contested areas, providing additional sensing and targeting capacity, or forcing an adversary to expend valuable air defense resources. The two internal weapons bays provide the means to carry air-to-surface munitions while retaining the aircraft’s low-observable configuration. However, we don’t know which specific weapons have been integrated, their quantities, or whether the GJ-11 can employ dedicated anti-radiation weapons for SEAD missions. Alternative SEAD/DEAD loads could include multiple Small Diameter Bomb (SDB) equivalents, including those that are networked, as we have seen in previous concept videos . Many other types of standoff weapons could also be carried, with the platform itself using onboard sensors for fixing the target or acquiring targeting information from other sources via a tactical data network. Overhead view of a GJ-11 outside the hangar. PLA screencap First live-fire strike claim According to CCTV , the GJ-11 has completed its first live-fire strike mission, with two members of the PLAAF’s initial batch of female drone operators participating in the operation. One of the operators, Shi Xiaoran, described encountering cloud cover that initially obscured the target. After circling once more, she located it and released the weapon, scoring a hit. A drone controller flies a GJ-11 from a command-and-control trailer. PLA screencap One aspect that remains unclear is the extent to which the aircraft can independently identify and engage targets. A successful strike would demonstrate weapons employment, but not necessarily autonomous targeting or engagement. A view of a GJ-11 showing its triangular engine intake and undernose sensor installation. PLA screencap Manned-unmanned teaming with J-16 and J-20 fighters Perhaps the most strategically important aspect of the new coverage is its emphasis on manned-unmanned teaming. The CCTV footage showed mission planning involving a GJ-11 operating alongside J-16 Flanker multirole fighters and, in a separate sequence, J-20 fifth-generation stealth fighters. This provides a more explicit indication of the role China envisions for the GJ-11 within its broader combat aviation ecosystem. The J-16 provides a powerful multirole platform for strike and electronic warfare-related missions , while the J-20 offers a stealthy crewed counterpart for operations in highly contested airspace. An uncrewed aircraft operating alongside either type could extend the formation’s sensor coverage, carry additional weapons, conduct reconnaissance, or undertake particularly hazardous missions. A J-16D electronic warfare aircraft. via Chinese internet As a loyal wingman, the GJ-11’s role would extend beyond simply carrying weapons, with the UCAV able to act as an additional airborne sensor and strike platform, allowing crewed aircraft to distribute tasks across a larger formation. At the same time, the footage does not establish how the UCAVs communicate with their crewed counterparts, how targeting information is shared, or the level of autonomy available to the GJ-11. The new footage shows the drone being flown under man-in-the-loop (MITL) direct control, but it likely features, or will feature, semi-autonomous control modes, especially for teaming applications, which will require a high degree of onboard autonomy. We do know that China expects the UCAV to be controlled by crewed aircraft, as part of its basic concept. The PLAAF has at least trialed crewed aircraft as drone controllers , and this is one mission set that has frequently been ascribed to the two-seat J-20S . A stock photo of the two-seat J-20S. via X From prototype to operational platform After years of development involving the experimental Sharp Sword design , the much more evolved GJ-11 platform was publicly unveiled during China’s National Day military parade in Beijing in October 2019. Its development is associated with Hongdu Aviation Industry Group, part of the broader AVIC aviation-industrial structure. Two views of an early Sharp Sword UCAV demonstrator. via X A model displayed by AVIC at Airshow China in 2021 provided an early indication of the aircraft’s internal weapons-carrying arrangement. In November 2025, as we reported at the time , the PLAAF released footage of the GJ-11 flying alongside a J-20 and a J-16D electronic warfare aircraft, suggesting that it may have entered service or was at least being integrated into the service’s broader air combat architecture. A screencap from an earlier video showing a GJ-11 flying alongside a J-16D and a J-20. PLA screencap Development and testing of the GJ-11 have been underway for years, with notable activity at China’s secretive Malan test facility in Xinjiang. Satellite imagery reviewed by TWZ has documented repeated, and at times near-daily, GJ-11 activity there, including multiple aircraft operating together. The deployment of three GJ-11s to Shigatse in Tibet between August and September 2025 provided an additional indication that the program was moving beyond test work toward operational evaluation. Two GJ-11s seen on the ramp at Malan on July 12, 2024. PHOTO © 2024 PLANET LABS INC. ALL RIGHTS RESERVED. REPRINTED BY PERMISSION Another image circulating on Chinese social media shows three additional GJ-11s parked alongside another example of the same type. Three GJ-11s in a hangar. PLA screencap Another hangar view with likely a fourth GJ-11 just visible on the right. PLA screencap According to Andreas Rupprecht, an expert on Chinese aviation and contributor to TWZ , numbers that can be seen on the drones themselves likely point to these aircraft being low-rate initial production (LRIP) examples. And what’s even more interesting is that, for the first time, numbers are clearly visible which – and I’m going to go out on a limb here – I believe are not serial numbers but rather design numbers. The numbers 0003, 0011 and 0012 are visible, so these are probably LRIP aircraft. pic.twitter.com/zH2D2Narr9 — @Rupprecht_A (@RupprechtDeino) November 10, 2026 The new releases come less than a month after China announced that the GJ-21 naval derivative had completed its first launch and recovery aboard the new Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan , which is equipped with an electromagnetic catapult and arresting gear. The milestone would pave the way for the PLA Navy to field a shipborne stealth UCAV for strike and reconnaissance missions. However, China has yet to release actual footage of the claimed operation, leaving it independently unverified. The Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan seen leaving Hudong-Zhonghua Shipyard for its first sea trials. Government of the People’s Republic of China The broader significance of the GJ-11 lies in the fact that it’s a genuine UCAV, not simply a loyal wingman designed to accompany a crewed fighter . Free of the endurance limitations imposed by a human crew, a platform of this class could likely offer at least twice the combat radius of a comparable crewed fighter. More importantly, it is intended to have the autonomy to conduct tactical missions independently, as well as operate alongside crewed aircraft. That opens up the possibility of extending China’s strike and reconnaissance reach considerably beyond what its existing low-observable crewed combat aircraft can achieve. The GJ-11’s flying-wing configuration, internal weapons bays, and emphasis on signature reduction suggest a platform approaching the very-low-observable (VLO) category. At the same time, China is now openly fielding a capability that the United States has conspicuously failed to bring into public operational service. In the late 2000s and early 2010s, the United States appeared to be leading the way in stealth UCAV development, with programs such as the Boeing Phantom Ray , X-45 , and X-47B demonstrating the potential of autonomous, long-range penetrating aircraft. Yet those ambitions effectively disappeared from the publicly acknowledged force-development agenda. The Pentagon has instead concentrated on lower-end and less capable Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA), generally designed to operate in conjunction with crewed fighters . Northrop Grumman’s X-47B UCAV demonstrator. U.S. Navy Northrop Grumman’s much larger X-47B that also featured a ‘cranked kite’ planform. USN As we argued in our earlier examinations of the American UCAV gap , the absence of a publicly acknowledged, sizeable force of independent, long-range stealth combat drones remains a significant weakness in U.S. airpower planning. Classified programs may exist, and the U.S. military certainly operates highly sophisticated stealthy uncrewed reconnaissance platforms , but even a small clandestine combat capability would be unlikely to make a decisive difference in a major, sustained conflict. China, meanwhile, is moving towards making this class of aircraft a central part of its military inventory. Important questions about the GJ-11 remain, particularly regarding its actual weapons load, various specifications, its degree of autonomy, and its ability to operate in coordination with crewed fighters. However, the latest official coverage provides the clearest indication yet of how China intends to employ its stealth UCAV in a future conflict, and sheds a little more light on the Mystery Dragon. Contact the author: thomas@thewarzone.com The post China Lifts The Veil On Its GJ-11 Mysterious Dragon Stealth UCAV appeared first on TWZ .

title: RISC-V Open-Source Chip Push Puts Strategy Over Capability
zh_title: RISC-V 开源芯片的推动将战略置于能力之上
summary: 内容摘要：中华人民共和国 (PRC) 正在扩大对 RISC-V（一种开源芯片设计标准）的使用，并扩大其对管理该标准的国际非营利组织的影响力。近年来，人们越来越担心被切断与 Arm 和英特尔等西方行业领导者设计的芯片的联系。中国公司现在不仅为消费设备而且为服务器和数据中心制造 RISC-V 芯片，尽管它们的功能不如专有芯片。 V100 于 10 月推出，由国家支持的实体共同创建，被宣传为首款
content:
内容摘要：中华人民共和国 (PRC) 正在扩大对 RISC-V（一种开源芯片设计标准）的使用，并扩大其对管理该标准的国际非营利组织的影响力。近年来，人们越来越担心被切断与 Arm 和英特尔等西方行业领导者设计的芯片的联系。中国公司现在不仅为消费设备而且为服务器和数据中心制造 RISC-V 芯片，尽管它们的功能不如专有芯片。 V100于10月推出，由国家支持的实体共同创建，号称是首款完全符合RISC-V服务器标准的通用芯片。国家级政策文件传统上避免直接讨论RISC-V，但今年9月，《电子信息制造业“十五五”规划》宣布，要求推进RISC-V研发和产业化，开发人工智能（AI）RISC-V芯片。 RISC-V 为自力更生带来了明显的好处，并且芯片可以进行调整，包括针对军事用例进行优化。
然而，中国的分析师担心芯片的“玻璃天花板”，甚至国家 IT 替代计划也指出，在政府系统中用于替代外国技术的 RISC-V 芯片的份额“可以忽略不计”。 10月19日，深圳芯片制造商进迭时空与香山处理器团队在第六届RISC-V中国峰会上推出了新型46核服务器芯片V100。[1]其制造商宣称其是首款完全符合RISC-V服务器标准的通用芯片（21世纪经济报道，10月19日；科技日报，10月20日）。 RISC-V 是一种开源指令集架构 (ISA)，是处理器运行的语言。与全球几乎所有计算机和手机中使用的 Arm 或 Intel x86 等专有 ISA 不同，任何人都可以使用 RISC-V，无需支付许可费或需要其他权限。由英国和美国公司制造的 Arm 和英特尔处理器必须遵守这些国家政府实施的许可和出口管制。相比之下，RISC-V 主要由 RISC-V International 监管，这是一家总部位于瑞士的非营利组织，旨在避免此类漏洞。最近推出的服务器芯片代表了中华人民共和国（PRC）该行业更广泛的趋势。
北京最初在 2010 年代中期开始将 RISC-V 视为对抗西方技术霸权并扩大其在新兴技术领域结构性力量的一种方式（中国简报，2023 年 12 月 15 日）。此后，北京通过国家主导的政策支持鼓励其发展，从城市层面开始，逐步上升到国家层面。尽管这些芯片的功能仍然落后于西方竞争对手，但它们越来越多地部署在数据中心的服务器中，而不仅仅是嵌入消费设备中。从市政厅到五年计划 2023年以来，地方层面对RISC-V的支持已经明确，特别是在上海、北京和深圳等一线城市（中国简报，2023年12月15日）。北京经济技术开发区的目标是到 2030 年使 RISC-V 产业价值超过 500 亿元人民币（70 亿美元），据一些估计，届时全国市场将达到约 2200 亿元人民币（210 亿美元）（北京市政府，2025 年 1 月 3 日；中国日报）

Executive Summary: The People’s Republic of China (PRC) is expanding its use of RISC-V, an open-source chip design standard, as well as its influence over the international nonprofit organization that manages it. This follows growing fears in recent years of being cut off from chips designed by Western industry leaders such as Arm and Intel. PRC firms are now creating RISC-V chips not just for consumer devices but for servers and data centers, even though they are less powerful than proprietary chips. The V100, launched in October and co-created by a state-backed entity, is billed as the first general-purpose chip fully compliant with RISC-V server standards. National-level policy documents have traditionally avoided discussing RISC-V directly, but in September, the 15th Five-Year Plan for the Electronic Information Manufacturing Industry announced calls to advance RISC-V research, development, and industrialization, and to develop RISC-V chips for artificial intelligence (AI). RISC-V brings clear benefits for self-reliance, and the chips can be adapted, including being optimized for military use cases. Analysts in the PRC worry, however, about a “glass ceiling” for the chips, and even the state IT substitution program has noted that the share of RISC-V chips it has used to replace foreign technology in government systems is “negligible.” On October 19, Shenzhen-based chipmaker SpacemiT (进迭时空) and the state-backed XiangShan (香山) processor team launched the V100, a new 46-core server chip, at the sixth RISC-V Summit China.  [1] Its makers bill it as the first general-purpose chip fully compliant with RISC-V server standards ( 21st Century Business Herald , October 19; Science and Technology Daily , October 20). RISC-V is an open-source instruction set architecture (ISA), which is the language that processors run on. Unlike proprietary ISAs, such as Arm or Intel’s x86 that are used in almost all of the world’s computers and phones, anyone can use RISC-V without paying a license fee or requiring other permissions. Arm and Intel processors, made by British and U.S. companies, must abide by licensing and export controls put in place by those countries’ governments. By comparison, RISC-V is mainly overseen by RISC-V International, a Switzerland-based nonprofit that avoids such vulnerabilities. The recently unveiled server chip is representative of broader trends in the sector within the People’s Republic of China (PRC). Beijing initially began to view RISC-V as a way to counter the West’s technological hegemony and extend its structural power in emerging technologies in the mid-2010s ( China Brief , December 15, 2023). Since then, it has encouraged its development through state-led policy support, starting at the city level and moving up to the national level. Although the chips’ capabilities remain behind those of Western rivals, they are increasingly being deployed in servers for data centers, not just embedded in consumer devices. From City Halls to the Five-Year Plan Since 2023, local-level support for RISC-V has been explicit, especially in first-tier cities like Shanghai, Beijing, and Shenzhen ( China Brief , December 15, 2023). Beijing’s Economic-Technological Development Area aims for a RISC-V industry worth more than renminbi (RMB) 50 billion ($7 billion) by 2030, at which point the national market will reach around RMB 220 billion ($21 billion), according to some estimates ( Beijing Municipal Government , January 3, 2025; China Daily , October 22). National-level documents have tended instead to use the term “open source” to implicitly refer to RISC-V. In mid-September, however, the 15th Five-Year Plan for the Electronic Information Manufacturing Industry announced calls to “advance the research, development, and industrialization of RISC-V” (推进第五代精简指令集 (RISC-V) 研发与产业化), and to support RISC-V artificial intelligence (AI) and embedded system chips ( Ministry of Information and Industry Technology , September 15).  [2] Server Ambitions, Smartphone-Class Silicon RISC-V’s strength so far has been in cheaper control chips for appliances and cars, but newer chips signal data center servers as an emerging use case. The Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) calls the open-source XiangShan core the most powerful of its kind in the world ( China Daily , March 26). Beyond the latest processor from SpacemiT and XiangShan, Alibaba now offers a server-class design, the C950, that it says performs on par with Apple’s M1 chip, which it released in 2020, on a standard performance test ( The Register , March 25). Engineers usually judge how well a core is designed via a two-step process. First, they run an industry-standard test, which times how long a processor takes to complete a set of tasks, and turns that time into a score. Second, they divide the score by the core’s clock speed, which is the number of steps it takes each second, measured in gigahertz (GHz). The result measures how much work a core does in each step (see Figure 1). On this metric, PRC progress is substantial: XiangShan’s cores have roughly doubled since 2021. By SpacemiT’s own ratings, its chip’s computing power is between 50–90 percent of Nvidia’s similarly priced Jetson Orin Nano Super, which is used in robots and drones. Its AI engine also falls short of the minimum Microsoft sets for “AI PCs” (see Figure 3).  [4] RISC-V, therefore, does little to address Beijing’s lack of compute. RISC-V Buys Assurance and Customization RISC-V offers the PRC with two benefits: the assurance of sustainable access, and adaptability for military purposes, which would be risky use-cases for employing Western chips. The fear of being cut off from access to chips has been acute since Huawei learned in 2019 that its access to Arm’s designs could be suspended ( BBC , May 22, 2019). As an open-source architecture, RISC-V can be modified and tailored to user requirements. In some instances, however, this has allowed it to be adapted for military purposes. A team at Information Engineering University, an institution affiliated with the People’s Liberation Army, was able to customize command for data encryption to a small RISC-V chip, accelerating encryption by about seven times with only about two percent more circuitry.  [5] These benefits are another part of the reason why the PRC has pushed to deepen its influence over RISC-V at the international level. Chinese firms now hold half of the 24 top-tier memberships in RISC-V International ( RISC-V , accessed November 3). U.S. firms are deepening their stake in the RISC-V ecosystem too. Nvidia said in July 2025 that its CUDA software, the backbone of AI computing, would support RISC-V processors, and Qualcomm bought the RISC-V server designer Ventana in December 2025 ( The Register , July 21, 2025; Qualcomm , December 10, 2025). Conclusion Beijing continues to emphasize RISC-V to advance technological self-reliance and resilience. Although it is starting to use RISC-V chips in servers and data centers, the chips function at well below the capabilities of the most advanced processors. Analysts in the PRC have worried about a “glass ceiling” (玻璃天花板) for the chips, and even the state IT substitution program (信创) has noted that the share of RISC-V chips it has used to replace foreign technology in government systems is “negligible (微乎其微)” ( Sina Finance , April 7). It is nevertheless too soon to dismiss the hype over the PRC’s RISC-V development. RISC-V currently also enjoys support from U.S. companies. This makes the international standards that govern RISC-V an important battle ground in the competition to shape this arena of open-source technology. It remains unclear, however, whether the United States will seek to build a U.S.-led ISA ecosystem or discourage U.S. and allied firms from taking part in Chinese-led RISC-V projects. Neither option is cost-free, although if Washington does not take action, a key part of the semiconductor supply chain could end up being controlled by Beijing. Intel and AMD do not publish comparable SPECint2006 figures, so their desktop cores are set equal to Arm’s Cortex-X925, which independent testing by Chips and Cheese found to be within the margin of error of the fastest AMD and Intel cores on the newer SPECint2017 test ( Chips and Cheese, March 3 ). Panels B and C compare whole server chips. The first is the number of cores. Each core works on its own task, so more cores means more work at once. The second is memory speed, or bandwidth: how many gigabytes of data a chip can move to and from its memory each second. In large data-center jobs this is often the real limit, because even a fast core sits idle while it waits for data. The lower panels of Figure 2 compare other measures of performance for entire server chips. The V100 has 46 cores; Nvidia’s Grace has 72; and the top Intel and AMD server chips have 128–192. The V100 also moves data to and from memory at about half their speed. It draws far less power, however, at 120 watts, compared to about 250 for Grace and 500 for the Intel and AMD chips ( GitHub , accessed October 27). [4] Figure 3 measures AI performance in trillions of simple calculations per second (TOPS). Since AI models run on vast numbers of such calculations, higher TOPS values translate to faster AI. The left panel divides TOPS by the power a chip draws, in watts, to show energy efficiency, which matters most in battery-powered robots and drones. The right panel shows raw TOPS for laptop chips. Companies quote TOPS in different ways that can double or even quadruple the headline number, so the chart puts every chip on the same basis. Even if the SpacemiT processor reaches 30 TOPS, this is still short of Microsoft’s bar of 40. By The Register’s estimate, even Alibaba’s best design would roughly match Apple’s M1 ( The Register , March 25). [5] Zhang Xiaolei, Dai Zibin, Guo Pengfei, et al., “Design and Verification of a RISC-V-Based AES Cryptographic Acceleration Engine [基于RISC-V的AES密码加速引擎设计与验证],” Application of Electronic Technique [电子技术应用] 49, no. 2 (2023): 39–44. Results are from FPGA prototypes built on the open-source Hummingbird E203 core. The post RISC-V Open-Source Chip Push Puts Strategy Over Capability appeared first on Jamestown .

title: AIT and TECRO Strengthen U.S.-Taiwan Partnership Through New Taiwan Fellowship Program
zh_title: AIT 和 TECRO 通过新的台湾奖学金计划加强美台伙伴关系
summary: AIT 与 TECRO 通过新台湾奖学金计划加强美台伙伴关系 PR-2631 2026 年 11 月 11 日 AIT 与 TECRO 通过新台湾奖学金计划加强美台伙伴关系 2026 年 11 月 10 日，美国在台协会 (AIT) 华盛顿常务董事 Ingrid Larson 与台北驻美国经济文化代表处 (TECRO) 代表 Alexander Tah-Ray Yui 签署了一份建立台湾奖学金计划（TFP）的谅解备忘录（MOU）。 《台湾联谊法》获得国会通过并签署成为法律
content:
AIT 和 TECRO 通过新的台湾奖学金计划加强美国与台湾的伙伴关系 PR-2631 2026 年 11 月 11 日 AIT 和 TECRO 通过新的台湾奖学金计划加强美国与台湾的伙伴关系 2026 年 11 月 10 日，美国在台协会 (AIT) 华盛顿董事总经理 Ingrid Larson 和台北驻美国经济文化代表处 (TECRO) 代表 Alexander Tah-Ray Yui 签署了一份建立台湾奖学金计划（TFP）的谅解备忘录（MOU）。 《台湾奖学金法案》在两党广泛支持下获得国会通过并签署成为法律。今天，AIT 和 TECRO 签署了谅解备忘录，并与国务院教育和文化事务局协调，启动了该计划的实施。该计划的主要目标是扩大和加强美台伙伴关系，并加强美国官员在台湾和海峡两岸问题上的专业知识。 TFP 将在台湾各地建立一批具有语言技能、文化知识和持久工作关系的联邦专业人士。根据该奖学金计划，美国联邦雇员将花费长达一年的时间进行强化普通话培训和地区研究。培训完成后，研究员预计将在台湾议会办公室、部委、其他机构或办公室或台湾公共部门以外的组织工作最长一年。
国会议员以及美国国务院、TECRO 和 AIT 的代表出席了在弗吉尼亚州阿灵顿举行的签字仪式，与会者称赞该计划在加强美台伙伴关系和建立美国政府在台湾问题上的专业知识方面所发挥的作用。美国在台协会董事总经理英格丽·拉尔森 (Ingrid Larson) 表示：“TFP 反映了两党对美台关系的大力支持以及对以民间关系为核心的共同承诺。” 《AIT 和 TECRO 通过新台湾奖学金计划加强美台伙伴关系》一文首先发表在美国在台协会上。

【原文 English Original】
AIT and TECRO Strengthen U.S.-Taiwan Partnership Through New Taiwan Fellowship Program PR-2631 November 11, 2026 AIT and TECRO Strengthen U.S.-Taiwan Partnership Through New Taiwan Fellowship Program   On November 10, 2026, American Institute in Taiwan (AIT) Washington Managing Director Ingrid Larson and the Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office in the United States (TECRO) Representative Alexander Tah-Ray Yui signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to establish the Taiwan Fellowship Program (TFP).   The Taiwan Fellowship Act was passed by Congress and signed into law with broad bipartisan support. Today’s signing of the MOU between AIT and TECRO initiates the program’s implementation, in coordination with the Department of State’s Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs. The main objectives of the Program are to expand and strengthen the U.S.-Taiwan partnership, as well as strengthen U.S. officials’ expertise regarding Taiwan and cross-Strait issues. TFP will build a group of federal professionals with language skills, cultural knowledge, and lasting working relationships across Taiwan.   Under the fellowship program, U.S. federal employees will spend up to one year in intensive Mandarin language training and area studies. Upon completion of training, the Fellows are expected to work, for up to one year, in Taiwan parliamentary offices, ministries, other agencies or offices, or organizations outside the public sector in Taiwan.   Members of Congress and representatives from the U.S. Department of State, TECRO, and AIT attended the signing ceremony in Arlington, Virginia, where attendees praised the program’s role in strengthening the U.S.-Taiwan partnership and building U.S. government expertise on Taiwan.   “TFP reflects strong bipartisan support for the U.S.-Taiwan relationship and a shared commitment to the people-to-people ties at its core,” said AIT Managing Director Ingrid Larson. title: Hong Kong gov’t workers granted up to 12 hours of annual family care leave from January
zh_title: 香港政府工作人员从一月起可享受最多 12 小时的年度家庭护理假
summary: 根据一项旨在促进家庭友好型工作场所的新举措，香港政府雇员从 2027 年 1 月起可享受最多 12 小时的带薪年度家庭护理假。香港，一名看门人带着一个小男孩散步。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。公务员事务局在周三向立法会提交的一份文件中表示，所有政府雇员，包括公务员和非公务员，可从一月份开始放带薪假期照顾家庭事务，例如陪同家人去看医生、参加家长会等。
content:
根据一项旨在促进家庭友好型工作场所的新举措，香港政府雇员从 2027 年 1 月起可享受最多 12 小时的带薪年度家庭护理假。香港，一名看门人带着一个小男孩散步。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。公务员事务局在周三向立法会提交的一份文件中表示，所有政府雇员，包括公务员和非公务员，可从一月份开始享受带薪假期处理家庭事务，例如陪同家人去看医生、到孩子学校参加家长会、处理家庭紧急情况等。该文件称，虽然员工每年最多可以享受 12 小时的假期，但每次可以申请 1 到 4 小时的假期，未休的假期不能结转到下一年。员工需要提交预先申请表，无需提供证明文件，这是该局提出的简化审批程序的措施。文件中写道：“如果审批机关对申请有任何合理怀疑，或发现任何滥用家庭护理假的迹象，他/她可以要求申请人出示证明文件，并接受各种形式的文件，例如医疗证明、出勤单、学校通知等。”前往中央政府合署上班的公务员。资料图片：香港政府一站通。
香港领导人李约翰在 9 月的 2026 年施政报告中提出了为所有政府雇员设立家庭看护假的计划，这是一系列促进生育措施的一部分，包括延长一次性婴儿奖金和增加儿童税收津贴。该局正在与员工协商之前敲定该计划的细节，预计该假期将于 1 月份生效。 2025年，政府引入了育儿假，允许有三岁以下孩子的符合条件的员工每年享受最多三天的带薪休假。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong government employees have been granted up to 12 hours of paid annual family care leave from January 2027 under a new initiative to promote family-friendly workplaces. A caretaker walks with a little boy in Hong Kong. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The Civil Service Bureau said in a document submitted to the Legislative Council on Wednesday that all government employees, including civil servants and those appointed on non-civil service terms, could take paid leave to take care of family matters from January, such as accompanying their family members to medical appointments, attending parent-teacher meetings at their children’s school, and attending to household emergencies. While employees may take up to 12 hours of leave per year, they can apply for between one and four hours on each occasion, according to the document, which added that untaken leave could not be carried forward to the following year. Employees will need to submit an advance application form without requiring documentary proof, a measure proposed by the bureau to streamline approval procedures. “If the approving authority has any reasonable doubt about the application or sees any signs of abuse of family care leave, he/she may request the applicant to produce documentary proof, and accept various forms of documentation, such as medical certificate, attendance slip, school notice, etc.,” the document reads. Civil Servants going to work at the Central Government Offices. File photo: GovHK. The city’s leader John Lee laid out plans to establish family care leave for all government employees in his 2026 Policy Address in September – part of a series of measures to promote fertility, including the extension of one-off baby bonuses and increased child tax allowances. The bureau is finalising the details of the scheme ahead of staff consultations, with the leave expected to take effect in January. In 2025, the government introduced childcare leave, allowing eligible employees with children under the age of three to take up to three days of paid leave annually.

title: Chinese woman accused of spying on Nvidia boss entered Taiwan on Hong Kong passport
zh_title: 被指控监视英伟达老板的中国女子持香港护照进入台湾
summary: 台湾移民机构周三表示，在当局调查这一事件时，这名被指控在与英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋有染期间为中国从事间谍活动的女子使用香港护照进入台湾。这张来自 CTI 视频片段的屏幕截图显示，爱丽丝·黄（右二，粉红色）于 2025 年 5 月 22 日在台北一家餐厅参加由 Nvidia 首席执行官兼联合创始人黄仁勋（左二，黑色后置摄像头）举办的晚宴。照片：法新社。据报道，黄仁勋承认与新加坡 Megaspeed w 的中国前高管 Alice Huang 有染。
content:
台湾移民机构周三表示，在当局调查这一事件时，这名被指控在与英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋有染期间为中国从事间谍活动的女子使用香港护照进入台湾。这张来自 CTI 视频片段的屏幕截图显示，爱丽丝·黄（右二，粉红色）于 2025 年 5 月 22 日在台北一家餐厅参加由 Nvidia 首席执行官兼联合创始人黄仁勋（左二，黑色后置摄像头）举办的晚宴。照片：法新社。据报道，黄仁勋承认与新加坡Megaspeed公司前中国高管爱丽丝·黄(Alice Huang)有染，美国官员认为她为中国情报机构工作。北京否认了间谍指控。英伟达董事会周日宣布，已对该公司首席执行官兼联合创始人黄仁勋展开调查，他与黄爱丽没有任何关系。入出国及移民署署长林弘恩对记者表示，“我国政府相关机构已充分了解相关记录和信息”，并证实黄丽娟使用香港护照进入台湾。 “我们知道她所有的相关出入境记录。”一般来说，香港护照持有者比持有中国大陆护照的人更容易进入台湾，后者还必须申请特别许可才能前往台湾。额外的限制部分是由于中国与台湾之间的复杂关系，北京声称并誓言要将台湾置于其控制之下。
积极调查 台湾内政部长刘世芳表示，黄爱丽“确实入境了，但她目前在海外”。“如果我们知道她是间谍，我们肯定不会让她进入台湾，”刘在国会告诉议员。她说：“我们将审查我们的程序，特别是预筛选、临时抽查和访谈以及访问后措施。” “据我们了解，这名黄女士的通行证已被吊销，这意味着她不可能再次进入台湾。”黄仁勋于 2025 年 10 月 31 日在庆州庆州艺术中心举行的亚太经济合作组织 (APEC) 首席执行官峰会上发表演讲。照片：Anthony Wallace/法新社。台湾官员拒绝透露黄爱丽访问台湾的日期，也拒绝透露她访问台湾的次数。刘周二表示，台湾“国家安全部门正在积极调查此事”。 2025 年 5 月，台湾顶级科技博览会台北国际电脑展期间，黄仁勋 (Alice Huang)，又名黄乐 (Huang Le)，出席了黄仁勋在台北一家中餐厅举办的晚宴。记者站在餐厅外，透过玻璃门窗拍摄黄仁勋和一名身穿粉色连衣裙、名叫爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 的女子与其他与会者混在一起的情况。媒体直播显示，有一次，黄仁勋用手臂搂住黄爱丽丝，而她亲吻了他的右脸颊。

【原文 English Original】
The woman accused of spying for China during an affair with Nvidia chief Jensen Huang used a Hong Kong passport to enter Taiwan, the island’s immigration agency said Wednesday, as authorities investigate the incident. This screengrab from video footage by CTI shows Alice Huang (2nd R in pink) attending a dinner hosted by Nvidia’s chief executive and co-founder Jensen Huang (2nd L in black back facing camera) at a restaurant in Taipei on May 22, 2025. Photo: AFP. Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a Chinese former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who US officials believe was working for Chinese intelligence. Beijing has rejected the spying allegations. Nvidia’s board announced Sunday that it had opened a probe into Jensen Huang, the company’s chief executive and co-founder, who is no relation to Alice Huang. “Our government’s relevant agencies are fully informed of the relevant records and information,” National Immigration Agency Director-General Lin Horng-en told reporters, confirming that Alice Huang used a Hong Kong passport to enter Taiwan. “We were aware of all her relevant entry and exit records.” It is generally easier for Hong Kong passport holders to enter Taiwan than those with mainland Chinese passports, who must also apply for special permission to travel there. The additional restrictions are partly due to the complex relations between China and Taiwan, which Beijing claims and has vowed to bring under its control. Active investigation Taiwan’s Interior Minister Liu Shyh-fang said Alice Huang “did indeed enter the country, but she is currently overseas”. “If we had known she was a spy, we certainly would not have let her enter Taiwan,” Liu told lawmakers in parliament. “We will review our procedures, specifically our pre-screening, interim spot checks and interviews, and post-visit measures,” she said. “As far as we understand, this Ms Huang has had her permit revoked, meaning it is impossible for her to enter Taiwan again.” Jensen Huang delivers a speech during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit at the Gyeongju Arts Center in Gyeongju on October 31, 2025. Photo: Anthony Wallace/AFP. Taiwanese officials refused to share the dates of Alice Huang’s trips to Taiwan or say how many times she had visited. On Tuesday, Liu said Taiwan’s “national security units are actively investigating the matter”. Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was seen at a dinner in May 2025 hosted by Jensen Huang at a Chinese restaurant in Taipei during Computex, the island’s top tech expo. Journalists stood outside the restaurant filming through glass windows and doors as Jensen Huang and a woman identified as Alice Huang, who was wearing a pink dress, mingled with other attendees. At one point, Jensen Huang can be seen putting his arm around Alice Huang as she kisses him on the right cheek, press livestreams show.

title: Presidential Message on the Birthday of the United States Marine Corps
zh_title: 美国海军陆战队生日总统致辞
summary: 总统关于美国海军陆战队生日的致辞 搜索 选择类别 所有新闻简报和声明 所有总统行动 行政命令 提名和任命 总统备忘录公告情况说明书 发布评论 研究 所有简报和声明 总统行动 所有行政命令 提名和任命 总统备忘录公告情况说明书 发布评论 研究 两个半世纪以来，美国海军陆战队一直是美国精神的生动体现。带着荣誉、勇气和坚定不移
content:
总统关于美国海军陆战队生日的致辞 搜索 选择类别 所有新闻简报和声明 所有总统行动 行政命令 提名和任命 总统备忘录公告情况说明书 发布评论 研究 所有简报和声明 总统行动 所有行政命令 提名和任命 总统备忘录公告情况说明书 发布评论 研究 两个半世纪以来，美国海军陆战队一直是美国精神的生动体现。凭借荣誉、勇气和对维护和推进美国利益的坚定承诺，海军陆战队一再证明，无论困难如何，他们都会响应每一个召唤并完成任何任务。在海军陆战队庆祝保护美国并击败敌人 251 周年之际，我向每一位为我们的国家战斗和牺牲的海军陆战队员致以最深切的谢意，并向他们无与伦比的英勇遗产致敬。从我们共和国诞生之日起，海军陆战队就一直捍卫美国赖以建立的自由和自由的支柱。独立战争期间，海军陆战队出海夺取拿骚港，为大陆军提供大量军需物资增援。在整个第二次世界大战期间，海军陆战队在整个太平洋战区发挥了关键作用，对于美国在关岛、瓜达尔卡纳尔岛、冲绳岛和硫磺岛的胜利至关重要。
这些令人难以置信的“魔鬼犬”在美国历史上无数次冲突的前线服役，从未失败过保护我们国内外的公民，并在我们的对手面前无所畏惧地展示了美国的威力和力量。今天，通过我们勇敢的海军陆战队的英勇无私的服务，美国变得更加安全。美国海军陆战队的爱国男女不断提醒人们美国伟大和荣耀的真正源泉。作为总统，我是我国历史上最强有力的海军陆战队倡导者。通过超级情报的进步以及对导弹防御、下一代能力和造船的投资，我们正在为我们的海军陆战队提供击败美国敌人所需的一切资源，无论他们身在何处。在我的领导下，我们的海军陆战队员也回到家乡，得到他们应得的关怀和支持。我的政府恢复了退伍军人事务部的常识，使退伍军人能够寻求自己选择的医疗保健提供者，降低退伍军人及其家人的费用，并减少有害的积压。作为总司令，我将永远不会停止为我们的海军陆战队挺身而出，维护他们作为世界上最致命的战斗力量的声誉。在座右铭“Semper Fidelis”（意为“永远忠诚”）的指引下，美国海军陆战队在我们国家和全人类的历史上留下了自己的印记。
我们海军陆战队的坚定力量证明了美国精神的力量和美国武装部队的力量。一代又一代，海军陆战队忠实地充当了美国的捍卫者，他们将在未来的几个世纪里继续作为自由的忠实捍卫者。永远Fi！关于美国海军陆战队生日的总统致辞首先出现在白宫。

【原文 English Original】
Presidential Message on the Birthday of the United States Marine Corps Search Select Category All News Briefings & Statements All Presidential Actions Executive Orders Nominations & Appointments Presidential Memoranda Proclamations Fact Sheets Releases Remarks Research All Briefings & Statements Presidential Actions All Executive Orders Nominations & Appointments Presidential Memoranda Proclamations Fact Sheets Releases Remarks Research For over two and a half centuries, the United States Marine Corps has stood as a living embodiment of the American Spirit.  With honor, courage, and unwavering commitment to preserving and advancing the interests of the United States, Marines have proven time and again that they will answer every call and complete any mission no matter the odds.  As the Marine Corps celebrates 251 years of protecting America and defeating her enemies, I extend my deepest gratitude to every Marine who has fought and sacrificed for our Nation and pay tribute to their unmatched legacy of valor. From the dawn of our Republic, Marines have defended the pillars of freedom and liberty that America was founded upon.  During the Revolutionary War, Marines took to the sea to seize the port of Nassau and reinforce the Continental Army with large quantities of military supplies.  Throughout World War II, Marines played a critical role across the Pacific Theater and were essential to American victories at Guam, Guadalcanal, Okinawa, and Iwo Jima.  These incredible Devil Dogs have served on the front lines of countless conflicts throughout American history, never failed to protect our citizens at home and abroad, and fearlessly demonstrated American might and power in the face of our adversaries.  Today, America is made safer through the heroic and selfless service of our brave Marines. The patriotic men and women of the United States Marine Corps are enduring reminders of the true source of American greatness and glory.  As President, I have been the strongest advocate for our Marines in the history of our country.  Through advancements in Super Intelligence and investments in missile defense, next-generation capabilities, and shipbuilding, we are providing our Marines with every resource they need to defeat America’s enemies wherever they may be. Under my leadership, our Marines also return home to the care and support they have so rightly earned.  My Administration has restored common sense at the Department of Veterans Affairs, empowering veterans to seek the healthcare providers of their choice, lowering costs for veterans and their families, and slashing harmful backlogs.  As Commander in Chief, I will never stop standing up for our Marines and upholding their reputation as the most lethal fighting force the world has ever seen. Guided by their motto, Semper Fidelis, meaning “Always Faithful,” the United States Marines have left their mark on the history of our Nation and all of mankind.  The steadfast strength of our Marines is a testament to the power of the American Spirit and the might of the United States Armed Forces.  Generation after generation, Marines have faithfully served as champions of America, and they will carry on as faithful defenders of liberty for centuries to come.  Semper Fi! title: Keep US troops in NATO’s KFOR

content:
随着五角大楼最终完成对美国在欧洲的军事态势的审查，一项相对较小的承诺值得避免预算削减：即在北约科索沃部队服役的约 600 名美国士兵。他们几乎没有参与关于旅和数十亿美元项目的辩论，但他们在巴尔干地区保持了来之不易的和平，将他们撤出几乎什么也挽救不了，同时让莫斯科获得了廉价的战略胜利。驻科部队于 1999 年 6 月在北约指挥下部署，此前北约轰炸了南斯拉夫，以制止斯洛博丹·米洛舍维奇领导的塞尔维亚军队对阿尔巴尼亚人的暴力行为。科索沃于2008年宣布独立，但塞尔维亚在俄罗斯和中国的支持下仍然拒绝承认。欧洲态势评估是一项合法的活动。在多年来敦促欧洲盟国承担更多常规防御之后，特朗普政府正确地提出了一些尖锐的问题，即美国军队在哪些方面可以增加独特的价值，以及在适当的时间发展其能力和能力的情况下欧洲可以在哪些方面加强。但驻科部队是一项美国角色不易被取代的任务，因为它既是政治性的，也是军事性的，而且错误的决定可能会导致欧洲东南侧的不稳定。从威胁开始。即使在乌克兰遭受重大损失的同时，弗拉基米尔·普京也没有放弃破坏欧洲稳定的努力。巴尔干地区是欧洲的软肋，是一个备受青睐的舞台：煽动成本低廉，是一个分散西方对乌克兰注意力的地方。
