The following is a summary of major ship movements and exercises in the Western Pacific over the last week. In Singapore A U.S. sailor assigned to Electronic Attack Squadron (VAQ) 137 conducts maintenance on an E/A-18G Growler in the hangar bay of Nimitz-class aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71), Nov. 9, 2026. US Navy photo The Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group departed on Sunday from Singapore. The strike group includes aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71) with embarked carrier air wing (CVW) 11, cruiser USS Chosin (CG-65) and destroyers USS Paul Hamilton (DDG-60) and USS Decatur (DDG-73). Theodore Roosevelt , Chosin and Decatur sailed west to enter the Malacca Strait while Paul Hamilton sailed east into the South China Sea. Theodore Roosevelt , Chosin and Decatur are now in the Indian Ocean en route to U.S. Central Command. Near Yokosuka, Japan Indian Navy Shivalik-class stealth multi-role frigate INS Sahyadri (F 49), Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force Hyuga-class helicopter destroyer JS Ise (DDH 182), Mogami-class frigate JS Mogami (FFM 1), Royal Australian Navy Anzac-class frigate HMAS Stuart (FFH 153) and U.S. Navy San Antonio-class amphibious transport docks USS Anchorage (LPD-23) and USS John P. Murtha (LPD-26) sail in formation in the Western Pacific Ocean during Exercise Malabar 2026, Nov. 7, 2026. US Navy photo Quad Exercise Malabar 2026 wrapped up Thursday in the waters near Yokosuka, Japan. Participating assets were Japan Maritime Self Defense Force helicopter destroyer JS Ise (DDH-182), frigate JS Mogami (FFM-1), a JMSDF submarine and a P-1 Maritime Patrol Aircraft (MPA), Indian Navy frigate INS Sahyadri (F49), Royal Australian Navy frigate HMAS Stuart (FFH153) and a Royal Australian Air Force P-8A Poseidon MPA, a U.S. Navy P-8A Poseidon MPA and amphibious transport docks USS Anchorage (LPD-23) and USS John P. Murtha (LPD-26). Anchorage and John P. Murtha with amphibious assault ship USS Makin Island (LHD-8) and the embarked 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit form the Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group. All three ships departed Saturday from Commander Fleet Activities Yokosuka (CFAY), according to local ship spotters . In Yokosuka, Japan U.S. Marine Corps Marines, pilots assigned to Marine Medium Tiltrotor Squadron (VMM) 364 (Reinforced), fly an MV-22B Osprey from the flight deck aboard San Antonio-class amphibious transport dock ship USS Anchorage (LPD-23), Nov. 8, 2026. US Navy photo Anchorage returned to Yokosuka on Friday and is currently anchored offshore there, according to local ship spotters . RAN frigate HMAS Stuart returned on Thursday to Yokosuka after its participation in Exercise Malabar 2026, according to local ship spotters . Indian Navy frigate INS Sahyadri returned on Thursday to Yokosuka and departed on Friday, according to local ship spotters . Submarine tender USS Frank Cable (AS-40) pulled into Commander Fleet Activities Yokosuka on Wednesday, according to local ship spotters . In the Western Pacific A U.S. Marine Corps CH-53 Stallion, attached to Marine Medium Tiltrotor Squadron (VMM) 364, prepares to take off from the flight deck aboard San Antonio-class amphibious transport dock ship USS John P. Murtha (LPD-26), Nov. 9, 2026. US Navy photo Amphibious assault ship Makin Island and amphibious transport dock John P. Murtha are underway in U.S. 7th Fleet area of operations. In the Philippine Sea A graphic posted Nov. 12, 2026, by Joseph Wu, Secretary General of Taiwan’s National Security Council. Taiwan National Security Council graphic The People’s Liberation Army Navy Liaoning CSG is operating in the Philippine Sea waters east of the Philippine island of Samar as of Thursday, according to a graphic posted by Joseph Wu, Secretary General of Taiwan’s National Security Council. The CSG was last visually sighted in October. The Liaoning CSG previously included aircraft carrier CNS Liaoning (16) cruisers CNS Anshan (101) and CNS Wuxi (104) and destroyer CNS Huainan (123) but the accompanying ships to the carrier may have changed since. In the South China Sea (L-R) Able Seaman Maritime Logistic – Supply Chain Leah Locke and Able Seaman Maritime Logistic – Supply Chain Grace Reading lay wreaths during a wreath laying ceremony for Remembrance Day during a Regional Presence Deployment 2026 on Nov. 10, 2026. Australian Defense photo Royal Australian Navy fleet oiler HMAS Stalwart (A304) is operating in the South China Sea waters near Brunei on the Royal Australian Navy’s regional presence deployment. On Wednesday , the ship conducted a Remembrance Day wreath laying ceremony with Royal Brunei Navy offshore patrol vessel KDB Darulaman (08). In Guam The ROKN Joint Cruise Training Task Force, 741 second year cadets from three service academies and the Armed Forces Nursing Academy were in Guam for a port visit on Nov. 9, 2026. US Navy photo The ROKN Joint Cruise Training Task Force, 741 second year cadets from three service academies and the Armed Forces Nursing Academy were in Guam as of Monday on a port visit. The task force includes amphibious assault ship ROKS Marado (LPH-6112) and amphibious landing ships ROKS Ilchulbong (LST-688) and ROKS Nojeokbong (LST-689), along with embarked Republic of Korea Marine Corps (ROKMC) MUH-1 Marineon helicopters. In Kangwon Province, North Korea North Korea leader Kim Jong Un inspected the construction site of a new naval base on Nov. 11, 2026, in Thongchon County, Kangwon Province. State media Korea Central News Agency photo North Korea leader Kim Jong Un inspected the construction site of a new naval base on Wednesday in Thongchon County, Kangwon Province, located on North Korea’s east coast, state media Korean Central News Agency reported. In Maizuru, Japan Royal Navy offshore patrol vessel HMS Spey (P234) departed JMSDF Maizuru Naval Base on Nov. 10, 2026. JMSDF photo Royal Navy offshore patrol vessel HMS Spey (P234) departed JMSDF Maizuru Naval Base on Tuesday after completing a five-day port visit that began on Nov. 6. Spey with sister ship HMS Tamar (P233) are forwarded deployed to the Indo-Pacific. Near Yonaguni Island and Taiwan A Chinese BZK-005 reconnaissance UAV on Nov. 11, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office photo On Wednesday, a suspected Chinese Unmanned Aerial Vehicle flew in from the East China Sea, passed between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan and reached the Philippine Sea. The UAV then turned back when it reached a point east of the northeast tip of Taiwan and flew between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan to return to the East China Sea. Fighter aircraft from the Japan Air Self-Defense Force Southwestern Air Defense Command were scrambled in response. Also on Wednesday, a Chinese BZK-005 reconnaissance UAV flew in from the East China Sea, passing between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan to enter the Philippine Sea. The drone then flew south until it was east of the northwest tip of Taiwan and conducted a circuit flight before returning back the same way to the East China Sea. JASDF fighter aircraft from the JASDF Southwestern Air Defense Command were scrambled in response. Suspected Chinese UAV flight paths on Nov. 11, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office map On Thursday, a suspected Chinese UAV flew in from the East China Sea and entered the Philippine Sea, flying between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan. The suspected drone was east of the northeast tip of Taiwan before its track was lost. Later that same day, another suspected Chinese UAV was tracked from the Philippine Sea east of the northeast tip of Taiwan. The UAV flew north and entered the East China Sea after flying between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan. Japan’s Joint Staff Office issued a news release on the flights, indicating the flights were conducted by different UAVs. Fighter aircraft from the JASDF Southwestern Air Defense Command were scrambled to intercept. In the East China Sea A Chinese Y-9 Electronic Intelligence aircraft on Nov. 10, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office photo On Tuesday, a Chinese Y-9 Electronic Intelligence aircraft flew in from China and flew from an area south of the Danjo Islands in the East China Sea to a position northwest of Okinawa. After completing a patrol circuit, the Y-9 flew back to China. In response, JASDF fighter aircraft were scrambled. In the Miyako Strait PLAN destroyer CNS Qiqihar (121) and fast combat support ship CNS Hulunhu (901) on Nov. 10, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office photo PLAN destroyer CNS Qiqihar (121) and fast combat support ship CNS Hulunhu (901) were spotted on Thursday sailing south 60 kilometers – 37 miles – west of Kume Island. The ships sailed southeast between Okinawa and Miyako Island to enter the Philippine Sea. A JMSDF P-1 MPA of Fleet Air Wing 1 and a JMSDF P-3C Orion MPA shadowed the PLAN ships. In La Pérouse Strait A Russian Navy Kilo-class submarine, amphibious landing ship RFS Nikolai Vilkov (081) and tugboat Fotiy Krylov on Nov. 10, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office photo A Russian Navy Kilo-class submarine, amphibious landing ship RFS Nikolai Vilkov (081) and tugboat Fotiy Krylov were sighted sailing west 40 kilometers – 25 miles – northeast of Cape Soya on the main island of Hokkaido late Tuesday. From Tuesday to Wednesday, the submarine and ships sailed west through La Pérouse Strait, which separates Hokkaido from Russia’s Sakhalin Island, to enter the Sea of Japan. JMSDF fast attack craft JS Umitaka (PG-828) and a JMSDF P-3C Orion MPA shadowed the Russian submarine and ships. This post was written by Dzirhan Mahadzir.

title: Japan Pledges Drones, Coastal Defense Radar in Latest Philippine Defense Package
zh_title: 日本承诺在菲律宾最新的国防计划中提供无人机和海防雷达
summary: BRP Jose Rizal 与两艘日本海上自卫队舰艇进行演习。菲律宾海军照片 日本将在东京最新的防御计划中向菲律宾军方转让无人机和海岸防御雷达系统，以支持马尼拉的军队。日本驻菲律宾大使北川胜郎和菲律宾外交部长特蕾莎·拉扎罗周一签署了一项协议，涵盖通过官方安全援助计划提供价值高达 2700 万美元的国防转让。此次援助标志着首次通过
content:
BRP Jose Rizal 与两艘日本海上自卫队舰艇进行演习。菲律宾海军照片 日本将在东京最新的防御计划中向菲律宾军方转让无人机和海岸防御雷达系统，以支持马尼拉的军队。日本驻菲律宾大使北川胜郎和菲律宾外交部长特蕾莎·拉扎罗周一签署了一项协议，涵盖通过官方安全援助计划提供价值高达 2700 万美元的国防转让。据日本外务省周一发布的新闻稿称，此次援助标志着首次通过专用海岸雷达系统向菲律宾转移国防设备。该雷达将由菲律宾海军操作，菲律宾海军是日本类似监视系统的先前接收者。上个月在马尼拉举行的日本自卫队成立 72 周年招待会上，日本公司展示了各种打算出售或转让给菲律宾军方的海岸监视系统。这些雷达包括能够跟踪 24 海里外船只的短程系统，以及能够感知 140 海里外海上目标的功能更强大的多用途雷达。除了海域意识援助外，菲律宾空军还将接收型号和数量不详的无人机。 2025年夏天，东京通过OSA向马来西亚转让了14架Aerobo Wing AS-VT02A无人机，价值高达270万美元。
此次移交是马尼拉和东京之间的首次无人移交。此前，日本将TC-90涡轮螺旋桨飞机移交给菲律宾海军航空联队用于海上巡逻。日本大使馆的新闻稿称：“该项目对于进一步促进日本和菲律宾之间的安全合作、加强日本重要海上通道的安全以及维护和加强地区和平与稳定具有重要意义。”近年来，由于对南海和吕宋海峡的共同担忧，东京与马尼拉寻求更密切的防务关系。自 2010 年代以来一些最重要的进展包括承诺为菲律宾海岸警卫队提供 17 艘巡逻舰，以及日本自卫队作战部队抵达东南亚群岛进行演习。今年，日本军队与美国、菲律宾和加拿大军队一起演习，保卫吕宋岛北部的海滩。东京首次全面实战演习以在击沉演习中发射反舰导弹而达到高潮。新的国防装备转让指南也为前日本自卫队装备出售或转让给菲律宾军方开辟了新的机会。目前正在讨论将即将退役的阿巴库巴级护卫舰转移给菲律宾海军。

【原文 English Original】
BRP Jose Rizal conducts exercises with two Japan Maritime Self-Defense ships. Philippine Navy photo Japan will transfer unmanned aerial vehicles and a coastal defense radar system to the Philippine military in Tokyo’s latest defense package to bolster Manila’s forces. Japanese Ambassador to the Philippines Katsuro Kitagawa and Philippine Secretary of Foreign Affairs Theresa Lazaro signed an agreement on Monday covering the defense transfer worth up to $27 million via the Official Security Assistance program. The assistance marks the first transfer of defense equipment to the Philippines via a dedicated coastal radar system, as classified by a Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs news release published on Monday. This radar will be operated by the Philippine Navy, which has been the previous recipient of similar surveillance systems from Japan. At the 72nd Japan Self-Defense Force anniversary reception in Manila last month, Japanese firms showcased a variety of coastal watch systems intended for sale or transfer to the Philippine military. These ranged from short-range systems capable of tracking vessels out to 24 nautical miles to more capable multirole radars that can sense maritime targets 140 nautical miles away. Alongside the maritime domain awareness assistance, the Philippine Air Force will receive an unspecified variant and quantity of UAVs. In the summer of 2025, Tokyo transferred 14 Aerobo Wing AS-VT02A UAVs worth up to $2.7 million to Malaysia through OSA. The latest transfer is the first instance of unmanned transfers between Manila and Tokyo. Previously, Japan handed over TC-90 turboprops to the Philippine Naval Air Wing for maritime patrols. “This project is of great importance in further promoting security cooperation between Japan and the Philippines, enhancing security of important sea lanes for Japan, and contributing to maintaining and strengthening regional peace and stability,” reads the Japanese Embassy release. In recent years, Tokyo has pursued closer defense relations with Manila amid mutual concerns over the South China Sea and Luzon Strait. Some of the most significant developments since the 2010s include the commitment of 17 patrol ships for the Philippine Coast Guard and the arrival of Japan Self-Defense Force combat troops for drills across the Southeast Asian archipelago. This year, Japanese troops drilled alongside American, Philippine and Canadian forces to defend a beach in Northern Luzon. Tokyo’s full-scale combat exercise debut culminated with the launch of anti-ship missiles at a sinking exercise. New defense equipment transfer guidelines are also opening up new opportunities for ex-JSDF equipment to be sold or transferred to the Philippine military. Discussions are ongoing to transfer soon-to-be retired Abakumba-class destroyer escorts to the Philippine Navy.

Cronin 亚太安全主席 Patrick M. Cronin 是哈德逊研究所的亚太安全主席。他的研究分析了与美国在印太地区和全球国家安全目标相关的突出战略问题。
伊利·拉特纳 (Ely Ratner) 马拉松倡议负责人、负责印太安全事务的前国防部助理部长特雷弗·瓦格纳 (Trevor Wagener) 计算机与通信行业协会首席经济学家兼研究中心主任 马特·莫尔斯 (Matt Mowers) 美亚公平市场联盟总监兼 Valcour LLC 全球公共战略总裁印太地区、美国和韩国企业在支撑人工智能、经济竞争力和国家实力的半导体供应链中发挥着不可或缺的作用。然而，韩国在贸易、技术、市场监管以及对华关系方面的政策引发了人们对该联盟方向的质疑。这些政策将如何影响华盛顿和首尔之间的信任与合作？公平对待美国企业、加强技术合作伙伴关系和更紧密的战略联盟需要什么？加入哈德逊研究所，与 David Feith、Patrick M. Cronin、Ely Ratner、Trevor Wagener 和 Matt Mowers 讨论这些挑战。
讨论将考虑瓦格纳最近的计算机和通信行业协会报告《KFTC 的不平衡之手》，该报告探讨了韩国在针对美国、韩国和中国公司的竞争执法方面的差异。 相关活动 查看更多 查看更多 相关研究 查看更多 查看更多

Full Bio Ely Ratner Principal, The Marathon Initiative and Former Assistant Secretary of Defense for Indo-Pacific Security Affairs Trevor Wagener Chief Economist and Director of the Research Center, Computer & Communications Industry Association Matt Mowers Director, US-Asia Fair Market Alliance and President, Valcour LLC - Global Public Strategy Share: Share to Twitter Twitter Share to Facebook Facebook Share to LinkedIn LinkedIn The United States–Republic of Korea alliance is essential for confronting threats from North Korea, China, and Russia and sustaining security in the Indo-Pacific. American and South Korean companies play indispensable roles in the semiconductor supply chains that underpin artificial intelligence, economic competitiveness, and national power. Yet South Korean policies on trade, technology, market regulation, and relations with China are raising questions about the alliance’s direction. How could these policies affect trust and cooperation between Washington and Seoul? What would fair treatment of American businesses, stronger technology partnerships, and closer strategic alignment require? Join Hudson Institute for a conversation with David Feith, Patrick M. Cronin, Ely Ratner, Trevor Wagener, and Matt Mowers on these challenges. The discussion will consider Wagener’s recent Computer and Communications Industry Association report, The KFTC’s Uneven Hand , which examines disparities in South Korea’s competition enforcement against American, Korean, and Chinese companies.   Related Events See More See More Related Research See More See More

content:
发言人办公室关于七国集团外长巴黎会议的联合声明 媒体报道 2026年11月13日，加拿大、法国、德国、意大利、日本、英国、美国等七国集团外长和欧盟高级代表发表以下声明。正文：2026 年 11 月 9 日至 10 日巴黎七国集团外长会议后的联合声明 我们，代表加拿大、法国、德国、意大利、日本、英国和美利坚合众国的七国集团外长，以及欧盟高级代表，于 2026 年 11 月 9 日至 10 日在巴黎举行的 2026 年七国集团主席国法国会议上举行会议。 乌克兰 我们重申对乌克兰及其勇敢人民的坚定支持他们捍卫自己的领土完整、主权、自由和独立。我们完全声援乌克兰人民，他们每天都遭受俄罗斯袭击，影响住宅楼、民用基础设施和文化遗产，以及针对乌克兰和其他伙伴的恶意混合活动。我们谴责黑海地区针对民用航运的袭击行动，这对全球粮食安全产生了重大影响，并加强了我们对保障粮食供应链的承诺。我们重申支持美国领导的通过直接和认真的谈判促进和平的持续努力。
我们重申了确保全面、全面和互惠停火的重要性。相互停止对所有能源基础设施和黑海的攻击，以保护平民，减少对能源（包括供暖、水和卫生设施以及粮食供应）的干扰，并支持全球市场的更大稳定，这是实现公正和持久和平的重要第一步。我们重申，有关欧洲未来安全的谈判必须包括欧洲人。正如我们在埃维昂七国集团峰会上所承诺的那样，我们评估了向乌克兰提供防空能力、系统和拦截器、远程能力和许可证方面取得的进展，这些能力将使其能够增加军事生产并行使其固有的自卫权。我们仍然致力于继续并加强朝这个方向的努力。我们承认需要以协调一致的方式解决乌克兰 2027 年及以后紧迫的融资需求，以支持乌克兰。我们谴责朝鲜和伊朗向俄罗斯提供军事援助，以及中国提供武器、军事训练和军民两用部件，这使得战争得以继续。我们明确表示打算继续对这些国家采取行动。基于我们领导人在埃维昂达成的共识，我们讨论了对俄罗斯战时经济日益增加的压力，包括通过制裁。
我们重申两国领导人承诺在针对俄罗斯的制裁问题上密切协调。我们重申决心重点关注悬挂假旗的船只或无国籍船只，以及保险公司、石油贸易商和中介机构等结构性推动者，以进一步扰乱和威慑用于规避制裁的影子舰队。我们重申支持乌克兰能源安全和恢复力，决定加大资金和物资支持力度，帮助乌克兰度过冬季。我们欢迎为使切尔诺贝利新安全隔离设施的修复保持在国际议程上的高度重视而做出的努力

Office of the Spokesman Joint Statement on the G7 Foreign Ministers Meeting in Paris Media Note November 13, 2026 The following statement was released by the G7 Foreign Ministers of Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom, the United States of America and the High Representative of the European Union. Begin Text: Joint declaration following the G7 Foreign Ministers Meeting in Paris on 9 and 10 November 2026 We, the G7 Foreign Ministers representing Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States of America, along with the High Representative of the European Union, met under the 2026 French G7 Presidency in Paris, on 9 and 10 November 2026. Ukraine We reaffirmed our unwavering support to Ukraine and its courageous people as they defend their territorial integrity, sovereignty, freedom, and independence. We stand in full solidarity with the Ukrainian population suffering from daily Russian attacks affecting residential buildings, civilian infrastructure, and cultural heritage, as well as malicious hybrid activities against Ukraine and other partners. We condemned the campaign of strikes carried out against civilian shipping in the Black Sea area, which have significant consequences on global food security, and strengthened our commitment to safeguarding food supply chains. We reiterated our support to ongoing U.S.-led efforts to facilitate peace through direct and serious negotiations. We reaffirmed the importance of securing a full, comprehensive, and reciprocal ceasefire. A reciprocal halt to attacks on all energy infrastructure and in the Black Sea to protect civilians, reduce disruption to energy, including heating, water and sanitation, and food supply and support greater stability in global markets is an important first step towards just and lasting peace. We reiterated that negotiations on the future security of Europe must include the Europeans. As we pledged during the G7 Summit in Évian, we took stock of progress on supplying Ukraine with air defense capabilities, systems and interceptors, long-range capabilities and licenses that will allow it to increase its military production and to exercise its inherent right of self-defense. We remain committed to continuing and strengthening our efforts in this direction. We acknowledged the need to address Ukraine’s pressing financing needs for 2027 and beyond in a coordinated way to support Ukraine. We condemned the provision of military assistance to Russia by North Korea and Iran, and the provision of weapons, military training and dual-use components by China, which enables the continuation of the war. We made clear our intention to continue to take action against these countries. Building on the consensus among our leaders in Évian, we discussed increasing pressure on Russia’s war economy, including through sanctions. We reaffirmed the commitment of our leaders to closely coordinate on sanctions against Russia. We reiterated our determination to focus on ships flying false flags or stateless ships, as well as structural enablers, such as insurers, oil traders, and intermediaries, to further disrupt and deter shadow fleet vessels used to circumvent sanctions. We reaffirmed our support to Ukraine’s energy security and resilience, and decided to step up our financial and material support to help the country get through the winter. We welcomed efforts to keep the repair of the Chornobyl New Safe Confinement high on the international agenda, as demonstrated by the donors’ conference organized in Paris on 9 November by France, EBRD, and Ukraine. We also welcomed the ongoing projects coordinated through the Tallinn Mechanism under Italy’s Chairpersonship to support Ukraine’s civilian cyber resilience. Middle East On Iran, we commended the work of the regional mediators and reiterated our support for all diplomatic efforts aimed at reaching a lasting settlement that addresses international concerns over Iran’s nuclear program and contributes to regional security. We reiterated that Iran must never be allowed to develop or acquire a nuclear weapon. We urged Iran to stop its support for nonstate armed groups in the region. Absent a diplomatic solution, we committed to continuing our coordination to economically and politically constrain the Iranian regime’s ability to sow instability in the region and around the world. We strongly condemned Iran’s attacks against its neighbors and the disruption of international trade, energy security, and the global economy caused by the obstruction of transit passage through the Strait of Hormuz. We reaffirmed the importance of protecting civilians and civilian objects, and called on Iran to respect its international human rights and humanitarian law obligations. We called on Iran to cease its persistent attacks against civilian vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. We reaffirmed our commitment to the right of safe and free passage and our opposition to any tolls, fees, illegal costs, discriminations or any limitation imposed on maritime transit through the Strait. We underscored the importance of the defensive activities undertaken by U.S. Central Command in the Strait of Hormuz to demine the waterway and escort civilian vessels. We recognized that the multinational, independent, and defensive initiative led by France and the UK can play an important role in facilitating the resumption of maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz also by supporting the verification of the removal of all mines. We reaffirmed our commitment to fully implement the obligations under all relevant UN Security Council resolutions sanctions and related restrictive measures reinstated in September 2025 through the snapback mechanism under UN Security Council resolution 2231, and called on all UN Member States to do the same. We urged Iran to return to compliance with its international obligations, and in particular to resume full cooperation with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) in order to restore transparency regarding the nature of its nuclear program. We also expressed grave concern over Iranian involvement in violent plots against many of our citizens and territories. We recognized the United Kingdom’s attribution of Iran’s involvement in the incident at RAF Fairford on 27 September. Iran should be in no doubt that we are united and remain committed to safeguarding our sovereignty. On Yemen, we condemned in the strongest terms the unacceptable continued strikes carried out by the Houthis in Yemen and against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, including those on civilians and civilian infrastructure. We called on the Houthis to immediately cease all military actions and threats and refrain from any further escalation to enable a return to an inclusive political process. We expressed our solidarity with the Government of Yemen and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and reaffirmed their right to defend their security, sovereignty and territorial integrity in accordance with international law. We urged all actors, including Iran, to end their arming of and support for the Houthis, in violation of several United Nations Security Council resolutions. We expressed deep concern at the worsening humanitarian impact of the conflict and called for the protection of civilians and safe, unimpeded humanitarian access with the urgent opening of a humanitarian corridor in Taiz. We reiterated our call for the immediate and unconditional release of all humanitarian personnel, including the 70 UN staff who remain unjustly detained by the Houthis. We reaffirmed the importance of maritime safety and security in the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandab Strait. We shared the importance of continuing support to the Government of Yemen, including through capacity-building. We recognized the positive contribution of the EU maritime defensive operations EUNAVFOR ASPIDES and EUNAVFOR ATALANTA to restore maritime security and protect maritime shipping and the lives of seafarers in the Strait of Bab al-Mandab, the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden. On Lebanon, we stressed the need for all parties to fully respect the ceasefire and expressed support for implementation of the Trilateral Framework and of UN Security Council Resolution 1701. We reiterated that the disarmament of all non-state armed groups, foremost among them Hezbollah, remains essential to ensuring that all weapons are brought under the authority and control of the Lebanese state. We called on Lebanon and Israel to make progress implementing the pilot zones to allow for full and verifiable Hezbollah disarmament and Israeli redeployment as the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) deploy. We reiterated our support for the Lebanese authorities’ efforts to achieve the disarmament of all non-state armed groups and for Lebanese sovereignty and territorial integrity. As the mandate of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) is set to expire at the end of the year, we underscored the need for a robust, credible, and long-lasting security architecture in Lebanon in support of the LAF, in line with UN Security Council resolution 1701 and enabling further implementation of the Trilateral Framework. In calling for a strengthened LAF, we welcomed the establishment of the EU CSDP mission EU Support Mission in Lebanon (EUSM Lebanon). We called upon Lebanese actors to move forward in the adoption and implementation of financial reforms in view of agreeing on an IMF program. On Gaza, we remained committed to the swift implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 2803 and to accelerate humanitarian, recovery and reconstruction efforts aimed at fostering long-term stability. We unequivocally condemned the attacks committed by Hamas on the 7th of October, reiterating that Hamas can have no role in Gaza’s future and must decommission its weaponry. Israel must progressively withdraw from the Gaza Strip, under the conditions outlined in UN Security Council Resolution 2803. We stressed the urgent need for the safe, rapid, sustained, and unimpeded delivery of humanitarian assistance throughout Gaza and the opening of additional crossings, as well as the rehabilitation of humanitarian infrastructure and the protection of civilians. It is vital that all parties continue to engage constructively on the next steps outlined in the Comprehensive Plan, in pursuit of a political horizon for peaceful and prosperous coexistence, for the Israeli and Palestinian people, that advances Middle East peace and stability. We called for ending terrorist attacks and other actions which increase tensions and the risk of escalation in the West Bank. On Syria, we reaffirmed our strong support for a peaceful and inclusive political transition towards a united, sovereign and stable Syria, ensuring respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms for all Syrians. We stressed the importance of fully implementing the arrangements reached on the peaceful integration of Northeast Syria and reiterated our commitment to fighting terrorism. We expressed concern over the situation in Southern Syria, calling for the protection of civilians and respect for Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. We also reaffirmed the importance of supporting Syria’s economic recovery and reconstruction to achieve lasting stability and to enhance regional connectivity. Indo-Pacific We emphasised the importance of a free and open Indo-Pacific region which is prosperous and secure, and that protects shared principles including sovereignty, territorial integrity, the rule of law, and the peaceful settlement of disputes. We reiterated our commitment to upholding freedom of navigation and overflight in the region and called on States to abide by their obligations under international law, as reflected in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). We expressed our serious concerns over the situation in the East China Sea and the South China Sea. We reaffirmed our strong opposition to any unilateral attempts to change the status quo, particularly by force or coercion or any actions that raise tensions and risk escalation. We reiterated that the award rendered by the Arbitral Tribunal on 12 July 2016 is a significant milestone, which is final and legally binding upon the parties to the proceedings. We stressed the importance of maintaining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait. In the context of China’s increasingly assertive activities in the waters east of Taiwan, which threaten regional stability, freedom of navigation and the safety of international shipping, we reaffirmed our opposition to any unilateral attempts to change the status quo, particularly by force or coercion, or the threat thereof. We encouraged the peaceful resolution of cross-Strait issues through constructive dialogue. We also expressed our support for Taiwan’s meaningful participation in international organizations. We strongly condemned North Korea’s unlawful nuclear weapons and ballistic missile programs and reaffirmed our commitment to the complete denuclearization of North Korea, in accordance with all relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions. We underlined that increased cooperation between Russia and North Korea has serious consequences for European and Indo-Pacific security. We urged North Korea to immediately cease all assistance and to withdraw its troops. We reaffirmed our concern regarding cryptocurrency thefts and cybercrimes committed by North Korea and expressed the need to respond to its unlawful overseas labor program. We urged North Korea to immediately resolve the issue of abductions. We remain deeply concerned by the deterioration of the human rights and humanitarian situation across Myanmar. We reiterated the need for the immediate de-escalation of violence, the unimpeded passage of humanitarian assistance, and a genuine and inclusive democratic process that reflects the will of the people of Myanmar. Sudan We were alarmed by the devastating consequences of the war on the Sudanese people and the growing risk of famine in parts of Darfur and Kordofan. Continued fighting, restrictions on humanitarian access and attacks, including by drones, affecting healthcare facilities, displacement camps and the infrastructure civilians rely on for food are putting lives at risk, which is being compounded by the impact of El Niño. A year after the atrocities in El Fasher, we unequivocally condemned all violations and abuses against civilians, including conflict-related sexual violence against women and girls. We called on all external actors to cease supplying or facilitating armed, logistical, and financial support to the belligerents and to use their influence to encourage the warring parties to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure, lift restrictions on humanitarian access and support de-escalation, and avoid any action that could contribute to the conflict. We underscored that, beyond an immediate cease-fire, a peaceful and durable resolution of the conflict is essential to securing unity and long-term stability in Sudan. In line with the principles stated at the Sudan Ministerial Conference in Berlin in April this year, we reaffirmed that a credible Sudanese civilian-led, inclusive, and transparent political dialogue process that addresses historical grievances and respects Sudan’s sovereignty and territorial integrity is critical to securing a lasting peace. We demanded the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces comply with international humanitarian law, engage in negotiations including with the Quad with a view to reaching a permanent ceasefire, and guarantee rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access. We reiterated our full support to the work of the Quintet aiming to facilitate such a dialogue, in a process that should run in parallel to and in close alignment with efforts to secure a ceasefire. We call on the wider international community to support these efforts. Horn of Africa We noted with great concern the worsening security situation in the Horn of Africa, specifically between Ethiopia and Eritrea, which bears the risk of regional escalation amid rising cross-border tensions. We underlined the serious consequences further escalation could have for regional stability, already dire humanitarian crises, security and international trade, including in the Red Sea. We called on all parties to exercise maximum restraint, pursue diplomatic solutions, and ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access and the protection of civilians, especially women and children. We reaffirmed the importance of respecting the sovereignty, political independence and territorial integrity of all countries in the region. In particular, we supported efforts by the United Nations and the African Union to reduce tensions and to facilitate dialogue between the parties. Haiti We supported and welcomed the renewal of the Gang Suppression Force (GSF) mandate through March 2027, which aims to assist Haitian forces in restoring security and stability in Haiti. We also welcomed the renewal of the UN sanctions regime, which promotes accountability for individuals and entities who threaten peace, security, and stability in Haiti. We called for international support to strengthen the Haitian National Police and Haitian Armed Forces, uphold the rule of law, and combat impunity. We also called on all security actors operating in Haiti to prioritize the protection of Haitian civilians in all security operations. We stressed the importance of organizing democratic elections in Haiti and noted the postponement of the first round of elections to July 2027. Noting progress made by the government and the Provisional Electoral Council in their work to advance Haiti’s path to elected governance, we underlined the need to safeguard the credibility and integrity of the electoral process and underscored the responsibility of Haitian authorities to ensure their full and impartial implementation of the electoral decree. We called for concrete results that strengthen public confidence in the electoral process and contribute to a credible return to democratic governance. We noted with concerns regarding the participation of sanctioned individuals in the political process, which undermines accountability and public trust. The people of Haiti have a right to determine their future through credible democratic processes and leaders who serve the public interest with integrity. We remain deeply concerned by the ongoing humanitarian crisis, widespread violence, and reports of human rights violations in Haiti. We urged the international community to intensify financial contributions to the UN Trust Fund, recognizing that the success of the UN-mandated hybrid mission depends on sustained multilateral support to resource its operations. We urged critical international support for humanitarian assistance for Haiti, in order to address the multiple crises facing the people of Haiti. We also underscored the importance of laying the groundwork for Haiti’s economic recovery with the support of international financial institutions and other multilateral partners. We welcomed the World Bank’s Compact with the Haitian authorities as a common framework to assess Haitian-led reform efforts and strengthen accountability for results. We committed to working with diverse Haitian and international partners to promote greater coordination and complementarity of efforts. Cuba We expressed our concerns about the profound economic crisis and humanitarian needs facing the Cuban people, including shortages of food, fuel and medicines. We stressed the importance of improving humanitarian aid delivery mechanisms into and throughout Cuba in order to improve the welfare of the Cuban people. We called on the Cuban authorities to pursue and implement significant and meaningful political and economic reforms to advance prosperity, respect for human rights, and the legitimate aspirations of the Cuban people, and to take concrete steps towards multi-party democratic governance, press freedom, and freedom of expression and association. We also called on the Cuban authorities to release all individuals who have been arbitrarily detained. We encouraged constructive and inclusive dialogue in order to find a way out of the crisis. Venezuela We acknowledged the will of the people of Venezuela to turn the page on the country’s prolonged political and economic crisis. In this regard, we reaffirmed our full support for the ongoing reconciliation talks that bring together the interim government and the delegation representing the National Assembly elected in 2015 and which have already yielded measurable progress. We called on all parties to continue to engage in good faith on the path leading from the restoration of institutions and the rule of law to the holding of free and fair elections. We emphasised the particular importance of providing guarantees to all parties and civil society organizations to enable their participation in the democratic process. We called for the release of all political prisoners. We acknowledged that Venezuela’s economic recovery is inextricably linked to the political reconciliation process and encouraged investments and commercial deals that help build a more stable and prosperous future for the Venezuelan people. We also offered emergency humanitarian response and civil protection activities following the devastating twin earthquakes on June 24, 2026. UN reform and efficiency of humanitarian assistance Committed to making the UN more efficient and effective, accountable and impactful, we welcomed ongoing efforts under the UN80, as well as humanitarian reform initiatives, including the Humanitarian Reset. These latter initiatives aim to strengthen the humanitarian system through better coordination, mandate delineation, and consolidation of common services and critical enablers, while remaining fully open to all impartial humanitarian actors and in full compliance with international law and the UN Charter. We reiterated the importance of maintaining sustained momentum in driving forward reform at this critical juncture for the UN. We commended the work of the G7 working group on the efficiency of the humanitarian supply chain (LOG+7), which is one of the most strategic drivers to increase the impact of assistance in a context of a significant decrease in financing and worsening of crises. These efforts towards a more integrated supply chain, including the reinforcement of the existing humanitarian hubs and pooling of resources, will help reach a greater proportion of the population in need without budgetary changes, and thereby contributing to address growing humanitarian needs including food insecurity and malnutrition in all its forms. This work will continue within the framework of the Humanitarian Leadership Group on Supply Chain led by the European Union and through the UN80 integrated supply chain initiative. Food security and nutrition We stressed our commitment to food security and nutrition to address the consequences of conflicts and instability, and to strengthen food systems resilience. We called for continuing action to address the disruptions to food trade in the Black Sea in the context of the war in Ukraine, the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and the El Niño phenomenon. Together, in 2026, we mobilized 2.5 billion USD of international funding to address the crisis in the Middle East, adding to our long-term commitment to more resilient food systems and fertilizer markets. Forced displacement of people We noted the serious impact of conflict, violence, and instability on affected countries and regions, as well as on broader regional and international security affecting the security of civilian populations. This constitutes a driver of forced displacement and irregular migration, and exposes victims of human trafficking to acute forms of abuse and exploitation. Malicious hybrid activities We condemned persistent malicious hybrid activities by states and non-state actors aimed at undermining the security and stability of the G7 Members and partner countries, through coordinated and deliberate campaigns, including acts of sabotage against critical infrastructure, malicious cyber activities, foreign information manipulation and interference, and the instrumentalization of migration. Such actions risk unintended effects, escalation, and miscalculation. We reaffirmed our determination to act resolutely and in a coordinated manner to address hybrid campaigns, using all available tools to prevent, deter, and respond to these actions, irrespective of their origin, scale and intensity. We stressed the need to reinforce our common efforts and accelerate work on all relevant work strands, in order to strengthen resilience, enhance preparedness, and protect critical infrastructure. Transnational Organized Crime We expressed concern about the increasingly sophisticated methods, violence, and reach of transnational organized criminal groups worldwide, in particular those involved in drug trafficking, human trafficking, and migrant smuggling, and underscored the importance of international cooperation to strengthen maritime security, combat illicit trafficking networks, and dismantle these groups. We also recognized that online scams are a form of rapidly growing transnational organized crime that poses a threat to regional and international peace and security, and stressed the need to strengthen collaboration, including with the private sector, as appropriate, and to disrupt online scam networks, which may be linked to other forms of transnational organized crime. Maritime and port security We reaffirmed the absolute necessity of ensuring maritime safety and security, and of safeguarding freedom of navigation worldwide, in accordance with international law as reflected in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), in order to prevent any lasting disruption to global supply chains, particularly with regard to energy, fertilizers and food products, because this can seriously affect vulnerable economies and populations. We recalled the global pledge initiated by the EU of 12 October 2026 on maintaining the integrity of the international law of the sea “No Fees, No Tolls”. We also underlined the need to strengthen the resilience and protection of critical undersea infrastructure, particularly submarine energy infrastructure and telecommunications cables, and their landing stations, including through enhanced international cooperation, information-sharing, redundancy and rapid repair capabilities. We encouraged practical cooperation with industry to improve access to repair vessels, equipment and spare parts, and to facilitate timely authorizations and port access for repairs, consistent with applicable international law and national requirements. In order to strengthen operational cooperation across our key maritime ports or relevant authorities, we, together with Brazil and the Republic of Korea, launched the G7+ Ports Network to Combat Drug Trafficking. This network will help strengthen operational cooperation, the exchange of information and the sharing of best practices to protect our ports from drug trafficking, in coordination and coherence with existing initiatives such as the European Ports Alliance, the European Coalition Against Drugs and the Maritime Safety Committee, and with the support of international organizations, in particular the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime. We welcomed the work of the members of the G7++ “Friends of the Gulf of Guinea” group to create opportunities for deeper engagement with the Yaoundé Architecture for strengthening partnerships in the fields of training, capacity-building and joint operations, as well as our judicial cooperation to facilitate the prosecution of traffickers apprehended at sea. We welcomed the work carried out by the members of the G7 and Nordic Baltic 8++ Shadow Fleet Task Force and reiterated our commitment to enhance G7 coordination with partners to further disrupt and deter the global shadow fleet engaged in illegal, unsafe or environmentally perilous activities. Resilience of critical satellite infrastructure We also recognized the need to strengthen the resilience of critical satellite infrastructure, including satellites, ground stations and control centres, and their supporting terrestrial connections and power supplies. We encouraged stronger protection against physical and cyber threats and harmful interference, as well as redundancy and contingency arrangements to maintain essential services. Taking into account the interdependence of undersea, satellite and terrestrial networks, we encouraged cooperation among competent authorities and operators on risk assessment, timely and secure incident information-sharing, and preparedness exercises. Such cooperation should support rapid service restoration, including through complementary connectivity options for essential communications, while safeguarding sensitive information. Frontier models We recognized the opportunities offered by frontier models to advance science and strengthen our economies, while also noting the need to ensure the secure and trustworthy development of these advanced systems and models through adequate safeguards and human-centric adoption, taking into account that they can pose risks, including for society and economic security. We acknowledged that frontier models can be misused by state and non-state malicious actors, including for malicious cyber activities and criminal activities, or to acquire and enhance chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear or explosive capabilities. We recognized the importance of strengthening the security and resilience of frontier models to advance innovation, economic prosperity, and national security. The developments and issues are complex. That is why it is key that governments, international organizations businesses and academia engage in discussions on model adoption. We will pursue our discussion to advance a secure innovation ecosystem for trusted frontier model deployment including through efforts started with the Hiroshima AI Process. Economic security and critical minerals We reaffirmed our shared concerns regarding the use of non-market policies and practices and economic coercion, especially on critical minerals and their related dual-use items. We will work towards strengthening our competitiveness and addressing the root causes of our common challenges. We affirmed the importance of the G7 Coordination Platform on Economic Coercion to build a common response to economic coercion and further promote cooperation with partners beyond the G7. We further recognized the importance of maintaining and strengthening of our midstream and downstream industries’ competitiveness, including in relation to critical minerals, by protecting critical technologies and commit to working within the G7 and with partners to coordinate on policy measures for technology control. Recognizing the strategic role of critical minerals value chains for the economic prosperity and security of our countries, and in light of the high market concentration in certain economies in the critical minerals sector, we reiterated the urgency of reducing strategic dependencies and vulnerabilities by diversifying and securing trusted supply chains to build up our collective resilience. In that regard, we recognized the importance of the measures announced at the Evian Summit to ensure critical minerals supply chains resilience and security. We commended the expansion of the G7 Critical Minerals Resilience and Production Alliance which builds on the G7 Critical Minerals Production Alliance launched under Canada’s G7 Presidency in 2025. This expanded Alliance and other platforms provide a venue for cooperation within the G7 and with partner countries in order to facilitate discussion, support data-driven decision-making and foster coordination among members to strengthen diversification and resilience of critical minerals value chains. End Text.

title: Malaysia and Singapore step up Nvidia AI chip probes amidst Jensen Huang controversy
zh_title: 马来西亚和新加坡在黄仁勋争议中加大对 Nvidia AI 芯片的调查
summary: 由于担心可能规避美国对中国的出口限制，马来西亚和新加坡加强了对人工智能硬件运输的审查。据路透社报道，马来西亚已对命运多舛的 Megaspeed 子公司进口的人工智能硬件是否随后出口到其他国家展开调查。与此同时，据《海峡时报》报道，新加坡已对另一名高管提出指控，指控其购买的 917 台服务器存在问题，这些服务器可能包含 Nvidia 加速器。此前，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋因声称拥有多个额外职位而辞职。
content:
由于担心可能规避美国对中国的出口限制，马来西亚和新加坡加强了对人工智能硬件运输的审查。据路透社报道，马来西亚已对命运多舛的 Megaspeed 子公司进口的人工智能硬件是否随后出口到其他国家展开调查。与此同时，据《海峡时报》报道，新加坡已对另一名高管提出指控，指控其购买的 917 台服务器存在问题，这些服务器可能包含 Nvidia 加速器。在此消息发布之前，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋因声称自己有多次婚外情而辞职，其中包括与一名可能协助 GPU 走私到中国的中国情报人员发生婚外情。分析人士推测，系统性芯片走私可能是他离职的原因。深入了解 TH Premium：台湾、贸易和关税（图片来源：台积电） 虽然美国在芯片制裁上反复无常，但中国正在建立自己的芯片供应市场 中国长达十年的半导体推动状况 华为 Ascend NPU 路线图审查了中国长鑫存储的目标，到 2030 年，第六座大型晶圆厂将占据 30% 的 DRAM 内存市场份额 中国最新一轮稀土出口管制解释说，马来西亚投资、贸易和工业部正在研究是否总部位于新加坡的 Megaspeed 的马来西亚子公司 Speedmatrix 重新出口了其进口的所有人工智能处理器和服务器，供当地数据中心使用。
显然，经过数月的调查，当局尚未查明是否发生过此类运输，如果发生过，是否符合马来西亚法律。马来西亚于 2025 年 7 月对美国开发的先进人工智能加速器的出口、过境和转运实施了限制，因此现在要求公司获得适当的许可证。马来西亚外交部表示，正在与海关当局以及新加坡和美国的官员合作，并可能推出额外的限制。总理安瓦尔·易卜拉欣表示，没有证据表明与 Megaspeed 相关的人工智能硬件已离开马来西亚，但他承诺配合国际调查。据 DigiTimes 报道，谈到 Megaspeed，该公司于 11 月 12 日表示，已聘请一家美国律师事务所对其 AI GPU 进行全面清查，并独立评估其对美国出口管制法规的遵守情况。该公司还证实，已配合美国商务部工业与安全局（BIS）的检查，并准备在必要时与其他美国政府机构合作。 Megaspeed 首席执行官 James Tan Yong Pong 强调，遵守美国出口规则以及透明运营始终是该公司的首要任务。
不过，Megaspeed没有透露其拥有多少GPU、有哪些GPU型号、BIS在检查时检查了哪些内容，也没有透露当局是否发现任何违规行为。 与此同时，新加坡当局已对曾担任Superphi董事、NJ Global Financial首席运营官的34岁中国公民石秉哲提出41项刑事指控。检察官称，这两家公司在 2024 年 5 月至 2025 年 2 月期间通过 41 笔交易从 Aperia International 购买了 917 台包含受限 Nvidia 硬件的服务器。当局声称，这些公司有理由相信这些服务器与 Aperia International 的犯罪活动有关。 Superphi现在面临

【原文 English Original】
Malaysia and Singapore have intensified scrutiny of AI hardware shipments amid concerns about the potential circumvention of U.S. export restrictions on China. Malaysia has launched an investigation into whether AI hardware imported by a subsidiary of the ill-fated Megaspeed was subsequently exported to other countries, reports Reuters . Meanwhile, Singapore has charged another executive over questionable purchases of 917 servers that may contain Nvidia accelerators, according to The Straits Times . The news follows the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over claims he had multiple extra-marital affairs , including with a possible Chinese intelligence asset who facilitated GPU smuggling into China. Analysts speculate that systematic chip smuggling may be the reason behind his departure . Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc) While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply market The state of China's decade-long semiconductor push Huawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fab China's latest round of rare-earth export controls explained Malaysia's Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry is examining whether Speedmatrix, the Malaysian subsidiary of Singapore-based Megaspeed , re-exported any of the AI processors and servers it had imported for use in local data centers. Apparently, after months of investigating, authorities have yet to find out whether any such shipments occurred and, if they did, whether they complied with Malaysian laws. Malaysia introduced restrictions on the export, transit, and trans-shipment of advanced U.S.-developed AI accelerators in July 2025, so it now requires companies to obtain appropriate permits. The Malaysian ministry said it was cooperating with customs authorities as well as officials in Singapore and the U.S., and could introduce additional restrictions. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said there was no evidence that Megaspeed-related AI hardware had left Malaysia, but he promised to cooperate with international investigations. Speaking of Megaspeed, the company said on November 12 that it had hired a U.S. law firm to conduct a comprehensive inventory of its AI GPUs and independently assess its compliance with U.S. export-control regulations, reports DigiTimes . The company also confirmed that it had cooperated with inspections by the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) and was prepared to cooperate with other U.S. government agencies if necessary. James Tan Yong Pong, chief executive of Megaspeed, stressed that compliance with U.S. export rules as well as transparent operations were always a priority for the company. However, Megaspeed did not disclose how many GPUs it owns and which GPU models it has, what BIS examined during its inspections, or whether the authorities had identified any violations. Meanwhile, Singaporean authorities have brought 41 criminal charges against Shi Bingzhe, a 34-year-old Chinese citizen who served as director of Superphi and chief operating officer of NJ Global Financial. The two companies purchased 917 servers containing restricted Nvidia hardware from Aperia International in 41 transactions between May 2024 and February 2025, according to prosecutors. Authorities allege that the companies had reason to believe the servers were linked to criminal activity by Aperia International. Superphi now faces six charges, while NJ Global Financial faces 35. The latest charges expand a case that now involves five individuals and six companies. Four firms — Aperia International, A-Speed Infotech, Aperia Cloud Services (II), and Luxuriate Your Life — were charged in July over allegedly making false claims when purchasing servers. Meanwhile, the exact nature of those claims was not disclosed in the report. Authorities have frozen the disposal of a property worth approximately S$55 million and confiscated around S$1 million from bank accounts. Shi faces up to 10 years in prison and a fine of S$500,000 per charge if convicted. His next court appearance is scheduled for January 4, 2027. The two cases largely highlight the significance of Malaysia and Singapore in the supply chain of restricted AI hardware to places where it should not be, such as China. Singapore's investigation focuses on alleged fraud and transactions involving proceeds of criminal activity, whereas Malaysia seeks to find out whether imported AI equipment was subsequently shipped abroad in violation of local regulations. Neither investigation has found that the hardware ultimately reached China, but both illustrate difficulties that authorities face as they attempt to enforce restrictions on advanced AI hardware across international supply chains.

title: ‘Broken and shattered’ Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang surrendered during resignation meeting, report claims
zh_title: 报道称，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在辞职会议上“心碎”
summary: 据报道，英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋在离开这家他创建了 33 年的公司时称自己为“一坨狗屎”。据彭博社报道，这位以其传奇般的精力和性格外向的举止而闻名的联合创始人在董事会会议上投降了，看上去“心碎又破碎”。在承认至少一次婚外情（其中包括与一名疑似中国间谍的婚外情）后，他从这家人工智能硬件公司辞职。但尽管他辞职并引发了围绕他的争议，英伟达员工似乎仍在支持他，该网站上有数千条评论。
content:
据报道，英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋在离开这家他创建了 33 年的公司时称自己为“一坨狗屎”。据彭博社报道，这位以其传奇般的精力和性格外向的举止而闻名的联合创始人在董事会会议上投降了，看上去“心碎又破碎”。在承认至少一次婚外情（其中包括与一名疑似中国间谍的婚外情）后，他从这家人工智能硬件公司辞职。据《连线》报道，尽管他辞职并引发了争议，但英伟达员工似乎仍在支持他，公司内部“意见箱”上有数千条评论，显示了对这位名誉扫地的领导人的支持。 “如果你相信使命，那就把老板带回来，”一位评论者说，而另一位评论者则写道，“我们都是人类，都会犯错误。詹森做了很多好事，他需要第二次机会。”一名英伟达员工私下告诉《连线》杂志，“英伟达因詹森而成为英伟达”，尽管另一名员工向全公司范围内发送了一封电子邮件，要求他的辞职透明化。 “我支持詹森。
不是因为我相信任何人都是绝对正确的，而是因为我拒绝相信维护公平就一定意味着与一个对我们来说意义重大的人保持距离。”他们还补充道，“如果美国辜负了帮助建设其未来的人，那么这个世界就不值得黄仁勋。”报道称，内部要求黄仁勋复职的呼声已在英伟达内部论坛上吸引了超过 1,600 条评论，“大多数人完全支持重新任命他”。该公司在全球拥有超过 42,000 名员工。有关 Megaspeed 高管 Alice Huang（涉嫌中国间谍）与黄仁勋关系密切的传闻于 10 月底首次流传，Nvidia 强烈否认有任何不当行为。 “Megaspeed 与许多其他区域云客户没有什么不同。詹森与黄女士的互动并不罕见或出人意料。与客户会面是首席执行官工作的一部分； Nvidia 发言人告诉 Tom's Hardware ：“Jensen 每年都会与数千名客户高管进行交谈。”然而，当有报道称他实际上与黄女士有染时，这位 Nvidia 首席执行官的情况变得更糟。此事传出后，Nvidia 总法律顾问兼董事会秘书 Tim Teter 在 Jensen 家中与 Jensen 进行了对峙，随后他承认了这一点。这位创始人很快发布了一份声明，承认自己的行为并为此道歉，同时公司董事会成立了一个独立委员会调查。
然而，另一起丑闻爆发，这位英伟达前首席执行官又与一名下属发生了外遇。这显然是压垮董事会的最后一根稻草，英伟达联合创始人不久后被迫辞职。报道称，黄仁勋是一位亲力亲为的领导者，公司有 60 多名高管直接向他汇报，而且众所周知，无论白天还是晚上，他都能快速回复电子邮件。但更重要的是，他是公司的代言人，特别受到很多人的喜爱，因此在他的祖国台湾产生了“Jensanity”一词。尽管他是亿万富翁，人们仍然发现他尝试街头小吃，在快餐连锁店吃饭，甚至纪念他在丹尼餐厅做服务员的卑微出身。除了这些最新的丑闻之外，许多游戏玩家还批评黄放弃了英伟达成为人工智能巨头之前支撑英伟达的核心市场。

【原文 English Original】
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has reportedly called himself “a piece of sh**" as he left the company he built over 33 years. Bloomberg reports that the co-founder, known for his legendary energy and outgoing demeanor, surrendered and looked “broken and shattered” during the board meeting where he resigned from the AI hardware firm after admitting to at least one extra-marital affair , including one with a suspected Chinese spy . But despite his resignation and the controversies surrounding him, it seems that Nvidia employees are still rallying behind him, with thousands of comments on the company’s internal “suggestion box” showing support for the disgraced leader, according to Wired . “If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss,” one commenter said, while another one wrote, “We are all humans and can make mistakes. Jensen did so many good things and he needs a second chance.” An Nvidia staffer told Wired privately, “Nvidia is Nvidia because of Jensen,” even as another employee sent a company-wide email demanding transparency into his resignation. “I stand by Jensen. Not because I believe any person is infallible, but because I refuse to believe that standing for fairness must mean standing at a distance from someone whose leadership has meant so much to us.” They also added, “If America fails the man who helped build its future, then this world does not deserve Jensen Huang.” According to the report, internal calls for Huang's reinstatement have drawn more than 1,600 comments on Nvidia's internal forums, "the majority in full support of reinstalling him." The company has more than 42,000 employees worldwide. Rumors about Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy, being close to Jensen Huang first circulated in late October, with Nvidia vehemently denying there was any impropriety. “Megaspeed has been no different than many other regional cloud customers. Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO's job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” an Nvidia spokesperson told Tom's Hardware . However, things took a turn for the worse for the Nvidia CEO when reports came out that he actually had an affair with Ms. Huang . Nvidia General Counsel and Secretary of the Board Tim Teter confronted Jensen at his house when this came out, after which he confessed. The founder soon released a statement admitting to and apologizing for his actions , while the company’s board formed an independent committee to investigate. However, another scandal broke out revealing that the former Nvidia chief had another affair — this time with a subordinate. This was apparently the last straw for the board, and the Nvidia co-founder was forced to resign soon after . Reports say that Jensen Huang was a hands-on leader, with over 60 executives at the company reporting directly to him, and that he was known to respond to emails quickly, whether it was day or night. But, more importantly, he was the face of the company who was particularly loved by many people, giving rise to the term “Jensanity” in his home country of Taiwan . Regardless of his status as a billionaire, people still find him trying out street food , eating at fast food chains , and even honoring his humble beginnings as a busboy at Denny’s . Aside from these latest scandals, many gamers castigate Huang for abandoning the core market that supported Nvidia before it became an AI giant, with consumer graphics cards now drastically more expensive than ever before. He was also often criticized for his all-out push on artificial intelligence and stance on selling chips to China . Still, those issues did not detract from his aura, with his trademark leather jacket raising nearly $1 million at a charity auction. It remains to be seen what will happen to Jensen after his monumental fall from grace, with SpaceX and Tesla mogul Elon Musk noting it would be an honor to hire Huang.

title: Mass smuggling of up to 1.5 million Nvidia AI GPUs could be the underlying cause of Jensen Huang's departure, analysts claim
zh_title: 分析师称，大规模走私多达 150 万块 Nvidia AI GPU 可能是黄仁勋离职的根本原因
summary: 领先的半导体研究公司 SemiAnalysis 认为，黄仁勋突然离开英伟达可能不仅是因为他个人婚外情被曝光，还因为先进人工智能加速器向中国广泛非法出口。在最新的时事通讯中，分析师估计，尽管美国实施出口管制，仍有超过 1.5 吉瓦 (GW) 的 Nvidia 受限硬件（相当于多达 150 万个 GPU）抵达该国。深入了解 TH Premium：台湾、贸易和关税（图片来源：tsmc）
content:
领先的半导体研究公司 SemiAnalysis 认为，黄仁勋突然离开英伟达可能不仅是因为他个人婚外情被曝光，还因为先进人工智能加速器向中国广泛非法出口。在最新的时事通讯中，分析师估计，尽管美国实施出口管制，仍有超过 1.5 吉瓦 (GW) 的 Nvidia 受限硬件（相当于多达 150 万个 GPU）抵达该国。深入了解 TH Premium：台湾、贸易和关税（图片来源：tsmc） 虽然美国在芯片制裁上反复无常，但中国正在建立自己的芯片供应市场 中国长达十年的半导体推动状况 华为 Ascend NPU 路线图审视了中国长鑫存储的目标，到 2030 年，第六座大型晶圆厂将占据 30% 的 DRAM 内存市场份额 中国最新一轮稀土出口管制解释 超过 1.5 GW 的 Nvidia 硬件受到管制根据 SemiAnalysis 追踪人工智能加速器生产和目的地的加速器模型，近年来美国的出口限制最终最终落到了中国。该估算不包括 Nvidia 专门开发的符合美国出口规则的处理器，例如 H20 或 H800。该公司还声称，美国商务部对未经授权的运输规模也得出了类似的结论。
然而，SemiAnalysis 并未透露非法运往中国的加速器的确切数量，也没有透露 Nvidia 各代产品之间的比例。所谓的转移规模尤其引人注目，因为现代人工智能加速器需要大量电力和基础设施。虽然该报告没有解释如何将加速器数量转换为功率数据，但该公司很可能使用封装级铭牌/额定功率乘以 GPU 数量。假设所有这些AI GPU都是额定功率高达700W的Nvidia H200 SXM，那么中国大约有214.2万个此类加速器，而如果所有这些处理器都是额定功率高达1,000W的B200 SXM，那么我们谈论的是150万个。对于混合部署，总数将落在这些数字之间，具体取决于 H200 和 B200 加速器的比例。为了将这些数字放在上下文中，xAI 的 Colossus One 拥有 220-230,000 个 Hopper H100 和 H200 GPU，而 Colossus 2 的目标是 120 万个 Blackwell B200 和 B300 GPU。也就是说，中国 1.5 GW 的受限 Nvidia 硬件代表着巨大的计算基础设施数量，与 xAI 现有的整个 Colossus 业务的规模相当甚​​至超过。虽然 SemiAnalysis 没有透露受限制的人工智能加速器到达中华人民共和国的所有案例，但它通过两起著名的涉嫌 GPU 走私案件支持了其评估。
第一个涉及 Supermicro 联合​​创始人 Wally Liaw、台湾销售主管 Steven Chang 和承包商 Willy Sun，他们于 2026 年 3 月被指控。根据起诉书，价值约 25 亿美元的服务器被出售给东南亚的一家公司，价值 5.1 亿美元的设备随后转移到中国并由阿里巴巴获得。检察官指控被告在审计期间使用替代服务器并转移识别标签来隐藏硬件的实际目的地。第二起案件涉及与台湾英伟达、青云、长电、飞虎和超微有关的九名个人。当局指责

【原文 English Original】
Leading semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis believes that Jensen Huang's sudden departure from Nvidia may have been driven not only by revelations about his personal extramarital relationships, but also by widespread illicit exports of advanced AI accelerators to China. In its latest newsletter, analysts estimate that more than 1.5 gigawatts (GW) worth of restricted Nvidia hardware, which could be equivalent to up to 1.5 million GPUs, has reached the country despite U.S. export controls. Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc) While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply market The state of China's decade-long semiconductor push Huawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fab China's latest round of rare-earth export controls explained Over 1.5 GW of Nvidia hardware subject to U.S. export restrictions ultimately ended up in China in recent years, according to SemiAnalysis' Accelerator Model, which tracks AI accelerator production and destinations. The estimate excludes processors that Nvidia specifically developed to comply with U.S. export rules, such as the H20 or H800. The firm also claims that the U.S. Department of Commerce has reached a similar conclusion about the scale of unauthorized shipments. Yet, SemiAnalysis does not disclose the exact number of accelerators shipped to China illegally, or their split between Nvidia's product generations. The scale of the alleged diversions is particularly notable because modern AI accelerators require substantial power and infrastructure. While the report does not explain how it converts accelerator quantities into power figures, it is likely that the company uses package-level nameplate/rated power multiplied by the number of GPUs. Assuming that all of these AI GPUs were Nvidia H200 SXM rated for up to 700W, then China got around 2.142 million of such accelerators, while if all of these processors were B200 SXM rated for up to 1,000W, then we are talking about 1.5 million units. For a mixed deployment, the total would fall between these figures, depending on the proportion of H200 and B200 accelerators. To put these numbers into context, xAI's Colossus One had 220-230,000 Hopper H100 and H200 GPUs, whereas the Colossus 2 has a target of 1.2 million Blackwell B200 and B300 GPUs. That said, 1.5 GW of restricted Nvidia hardware in China represents an enormous amount of computing infrastructure, which is comparable, or even exceeds, the scale of xAI's entire existing Colossus operation. While SemiAnalysis did not reveal all the cases in which restricted AI accelerators reached the People's Republic of China, it supports its assessment with two well-known cases of alleged GPU smuggling. The first involves Supermicro co-founder Wally Liaw, Taiwan sales executive Steven Chang, and contractor Willy Sun, who were charged in March 2026. According to the indictment, approximately $2.5 billion worth of servers were sold to a company in Southeast Asia, with $510 million worth of equipment subsequently diverted to China and obtained by Alibaba . Prosecutors allege that the defendants used substitute servers and transferred identification labels to conceal the actual destinations of the hardware during audits. The second case involves nine individuals associated with Nvidia, Albatron, Chief Telecom, Flying Tiger, and Supermicro in Taiwan. The authorities accuse the group of arranging unauthorized exports of 130 Nvidia B300-based servers, 74 of which eventually reached China. The suspects used shell companies, forged documents, and declared Japan as the destination for servers that were actually bound for China, according to prosecutors. Taiwanese authorities discovered the operation during a drug smuggling investigation. Both cases are still before the courts. Amidst the ongoing fallout and reports into Jensen's Huang's extramarital affair with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese intelligence asset who was an executive at Megaspeed, one report claims that Ms. Huang was personally responsible for facilitating the smuggling of $7.5 billion of Nvidia AI hardware into China , around 240,000 GPUs, mostly H100 and H200 models. The right timing? SemiAnalysis suggests that the scale of these violations may explain why Huang's personal conduct became a major issue at this very point in time. The company's analysts speculate that some members of the U.S. intelligence community sought to remove Jensen Huang because he opposed more aggressive restrictions on China's access to American AI hardware. However, the report provides no direct evidence that intelligence agencies influenced Nvidia's board or that Huang participated in unauthorized exports. The timing also coincides with congressional efforts to advance the Remote Access Security Act (RASA), which passed the House of Representatives on January 12. The legislation is meant to extend U.S. export-control authority to remote access to advanced AI hardware hosted outside China, including data centers in Europe and the Middle East. SemiAnalysis reports that Nvidia and Oracle have actively opposed the proposal. The analysts believe that Huang's departure essentially removes an influential opponent of stricter restrictions and accelerates efforts to block Chinese companies from accessing American AI hardware in the cloud. However, SemiAnalysis warns that truly all-inclusive restrictions could encourage Chinese developers to adopt domestic accelerators (something that Jensen Huang has consistently warned about), undermine international AI software collaboration, and ultimately weaken American high-tech companies. Continued Chinese access to American AI accelerators offers several advantages to the U.S. technology industry, according to SemiAnalysis. Firstly, it generates revenue for American companies such as AMD, Nvidia, and cloud service providers. Secondly, when Chinese companies rent GPU capacity from data centers outside China, U.S. authorities retain the ability to monitor their activities and potentially terminate access if necessary due to national security concerns. Thirdly, prolonged reliance on American hardware reduces incentives for Chinese developers to adopt domestic AI accelerators, which could eventually compete with AMD and Nvidia in international markets. Another important aspect is the contribution of Chinese developers to the global software ecosystem. On the one hand, Chinese laboratories have developed open-source technologies such as DeepEP, DeepGEMM, and MSA, which improve the efficiency of AI workloads on Nvidia hardware and benefit developers worldwide. In addition, American companies also depend on Chinese engineers, component suppliers, and manufacturers. Therefore, legal curbs that completely restrict Chinese developers' access to American AI accelerators could undermine international cooperation, reduce availability of open-source optimizations, and encourage Chinese companies to develop software specifically for domestic hardware. On the other hand, access to advanced AI accelerators from AMD or Nvidia enables Chinese laboratories to develop increasingly sophisticated AI models, which will rival leading-edge models developed in America and perhaps create national security risks. To that end, SemiAnalysis acknowledges the need to limit China's access to advanced AI accelerators from U.S.-based companies, as they could, among other things, be used to develop weapons of mass destruction or undermine American national security in different ways. Yet, SA analysts argue that restrictions should focus on the amount and capabilities of hardware available to Chinese entities rather than completely prohibit any access. SemiAnalysis seems to favor a system in which Chinese developers can rent computing capacity from trusted providers outside China under U.S. oversight. Such an approach could preserve American technological influence and commercial benefits and limit China's ability to acquire advanced AI infrastructure independently.

title: How Shanghai fund manager Kang Wei introduced his wife Alice Huang to Jensen and built $7.5 billion Nvidia AI GPU smuggling operation
zh_title: 上海基金经理康伟如何将他的妻子 Alice Huang 介绍给 Jensen，并建立了价值 75 亿美元的 Nvidia AI GPU 走私业务
